title: Clashes erupt at Lucknow University over Rohit Vemula march:BAPSA, ABVP face off after slogan row; police detain students to restore order
summary: Tension gripped Lucknow University on Saturday after student groups clashed during marches held in memory of Rohit Vemula. What began as slogan shouting soon turned into physical fights, forcing heavy police intervention and leading to detentions and complaints from rival student organisations. Memorial march sparks tension Students of the Birsa Ambedkar Phule Student Association (BAPSA) took out a march on the university campus to mark Rohit Vemula’s death anniversary. They gathered near the Ambedkar statue and raised slogans demanding justice and an end to harassment of students. Police were already present to maintain security. See 3 pictures - Argument over slogans turns violent During the march, a debate broke out between BAPSA students and another group over slogan shouting. Within minutes, loud slogans were raised from both sides, creating a tense atmosphere. Soon, BAPSA members and ABVP workers came face to face, and the argument turned into a physical clash. Police struggle to control clash The fight escalated quickly. Police had to work hard to separate the two groups and calm the situation. For some time, officers appeared overwhelmed as students continued sloganeering and pushing each other inside the campus. Slogans raised during protest BAPSA students shouted slogans such as, “Rohit, we are ashamed, your killers are alive.” They said strict action should be taken to prevent similar incidents in future and to ensure students are not harassed. BAPSA alleges attack by ABVP Later, BAPSA issued a written statement. It said that a peaceful “Rohit Smriti Yatra” began around noon but was allegedly attacked by ABVP and RSS workers. The group claimed students were assaulted and one student suffered serious injuries. Despite this, the march ended with slogans of Jai Bhim. Complaint filed by ABVP-linked scholar On the other hand, ABVP-linked research scholar Radheshyam Pandey filed a complaint at Hasanganj police station. He alleged that BAPSA workers attacked him while he was heading towards the university’s administrative building. He said the march was held without permission and involved a deadly assault. Allegations over objectionable slogans According to the complaint, slogans referring to Brahmanism, Thakurism and opportunism were raised. Pandey claimed he was targeted because of his association with ABVP and his caste. Police said vehicles were stopped during the clash and others nearby were also injured. Police probe and named accused Police confirmed that a case is being examined based on the complaint. Allegations have been made against BAPSA president Shikhar Das, Ram Sharan, Ravi and around 20 others. The investigation is ongoing. Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha march halted Separately, the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha also organised a memorial march for Rohit Vemula. Police tried to stop the students to prevent further unrest. This led to fresh tension between students and police on campus. Students detained by police Police dragged several students into buses and detained them. This action angered students and caused chaos for some time. Academic activities in the university were also disrupted during the unrest. Samajwadi student wing’s allegation Atul Kumar Shukla, secretary of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, alleged that the government was acting against Dalit interests. He claimed students were peacefully marching but police from four stations were called in to forcibly stop and detain them. Students raise democratic concerns Student leaders said they wanted a better academic environment and resolution of student issues. They accused the government of violating democratic rights by stopping peaceful protests. Heavy security deployed After the clashes, police increased security across and around the campus. The administration said forces remain deployed to prevent further trouble. Officials confirmed that the situation is now under control.

title: Famous Bollywood actor Pradeep Kabra reaches Varanasi:Seen in simple attire; sits on ghat steps barefoot; writes, 'I am lost somewhere'
summary: Actor Pradeep Kabra, known for his powerful negative roles in Bollywood films, arrived in Kashi. During this time, he made an emotional video at the Ganga Ghat, which is going viral rapidly on social media. In the video, Pradeep Kabra is saying that I have lost something. When asked what is lost, he smilingly replies that my mind is lost somewhere. After this, the video shows beautiful glimpses of Kashi's Ganga ghats. During this time, he appeared in simple attire. He also sat on the ghat steps without slippers or shoes. During this time, no tourist was able to recognise him. First see 2 pictures.. Harsha Richariya, who became famous from Mahakumbh, commented During this journey, Pradeep Kabra presented himself as a regular tourist. He explored the streets of Banaras and closely experienced the culture and spiritual atmosphere here. Along with this, he also performed darshan and worship at major temples. There have been many reactions on social media to this video of Pradeep Kabra, in which Harsha Richaria, who became famous from Mahakumbh, also replied to the video writing, "Deep Message". Seen touring the Ganga ghats of Varanasi Actor Pradeep, sharing a video from Hanuman Ghat in Varanasi, said - There can be many ways to live life, but the right way is one that gives satisfaction to oneself without causing pain to others. During this time, he was seen touring the Ganga ghats of Varanasi. Also news of Harishchandra Ghat, for the past two days he has been sharing videos of different Ganga ghats of Varanasi. Tourists are passing by him at the Ganga ghat, but they are unable to recognize him. Dressed like a regular tourist, he can be seen enjoying Kashi. Salman Khan's film gave recognition Pradeep Kabra is among those artists who have created their special identity in Bollywood by mostly playing negative characters. He got his real recognition from the negative role played in Salman Khan's film 'Wanted'. After this, he appeared as villains and goons in big films like 'Bang Bang', 'Dilwale', 'Suryavanshi' and 'Simmba'. Acted in South and Rajasthani Films Pradeep Kabra entered Bollywood in 2004 with the film 'Run' starring Abhishek Bachchan and Bhumika Chawla. After this, he worked in popular films like 'Delhi Belly', 'Bang Bang!' and Shah Rukh Khan's film 'Dilwale'. His acting was not limited to Hindi cinema. He has also appeared in Tamil superstar Rajinikanth's film 'Darbar'. Additionally, Pradeep Kabra played an important role in the Rajasthani film 'Taawdo: The Sunlight', which was praised at several film festivals. This video that emerged during his Kashi visit shows that behind the screen image of a dangerous villain lies an artist who is sensitive and in search of peace.

title: Female teacher found dead in Barabanki school:Body found hanging in Headmaster’s office; husband alleges harassment
summary: The body of a female teacher was found hanging in the headmaster’s office of a government school in Barabanki district on Saturday. The incident has sent shockwaves through the local education community, with the victim’s husband accusing the school headmaster of harassment. The incident occurred at the Composite School in Udhwapur village, under the jurisdiction of Satrik police station. The deceased has been identified as Uma Verma, also known as Mala (40), a resident of the Jalalpur locality in Barabanki city. See two images related to the incident... Sequence of Events at the School According to information, Uma Verma’s husband, Rishi—who is also a teacher posted at a school in Sidhaur block—dropped her at the school on Friday morning before leaving for his own workplace. After arriving, Uma reportedly kept her bag in her classroom and then went to the headmaster’s office. When she did not return for a long time, fellow teachers became concerned and called out to her. Receiving no response, they opened the office door and found her body hanging from a noose inside. Police and Forensic Investigation The school staff immediately informed the police. Officers from Satrik police station arrived at the scene, and a forensic team was called in to examine the site and collect evidence. The body was taken into police custody and sent for post-mortem examination. Allegations and Ongoing Probe Uma Verma is survived by her husband and their two children. Her husband has alleged that she was being harassed by the headmaster, though police have not yet confirmed these claims. Police officials stated that the matter is being investigated from all angles. The exact cause of death will be determined after the forensic analysis and post-mortem report. Meanwhile, statements from family members and school staff are being recorded as part of the ongoing investigation. The news is being continuously updated...

title: Video of Ahilyabai’s broken statue AI-generated- Yogi:UP CM calls it conspiracy of Congress, says queen’s statue safe; work halted at Manikarnika Ghat
summary: In Kashi, Chief Minister Yogi on Saturday blamed the Congress over the controversy surrounding the alleged damage to Queen Ahilyabai’s statue at Manikarnika Ghat. He said the queen’s statue has been kept safe. The Congress created a video showing the statue broken using AI. He called it a conspiracy to defame Kashi, which is why he had to come here personally. He said the conspiracy must be exposed. The Chief Minister said claims that temples have been demolished are completely false. He said Ahilyabai Holkar’s statue has been properly preserved. Once the renovation work is completed, the statue will appear in a new form. He alleged that the Congress is misleading the public by spreading AI-generated videos of temple demolition, calling it a criminal act. The Chief Minister said the Congress never respected Ahilyabai. He said the comments made by its leaders deserve laughter and pity. He compared it to a cat going on a pilgrimage after eating a hundred mice. He warned those creating images using AI, saying this will not be accepted under any circumstances. The controversy began on January 10, when the Holkar Trust of Indore claimed that the statue of Devi Ahilyabai Holkar at Manikarnika Ghat had been broken. It also alleged that several religious symbols were damaged and some statues were broken and buried under debris. After this, some images surfaced. At that time, the Varanasi District Magistrate described them as AI-generated. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav had also held the BJP responsible for the issue. At present, new construction work at Manikarnika Ghat has been halted. Meanwhile, the district administration and BJP leaders have denied allegations of any temple demolition. They have stated that an idol mounted on a wall was carefully removed and preserved, and it will be reinstalled with due respect once the ghat construction work is completed. Nothing is hidden from you… The Chief Minister said, “Whenever worship takes place at Kashi Vishwanath, the cremation grounds are also discussed, whether it is Manikarnika Ghat or Harishchandra Ghat. Even today, if you go to Manikarnika Ghat, you will see the conditions in which last rites are performed. How can it be acceptable that someone is unable to give their loved one a dignified farewell? For this, a programme is being launched. It is not being funded by government money, but through CSR funds of a company, made possible by the efforts of the Prime Minister. Even then, the same people have started their complaints again. What is happening at present is not hidden from you.” Congress did not honour Ahilyabai Holkar The Chief Minister said Aurangzeb had demolished the Baba Vishwanath temple. The first effort to rebuild the temple was made by Ahilyabai Holkar. Congress did not honour her, but Prime Minister Modi did. However, for the last three to four days, some people have been misleading the public by circulating false pictures. These are the same people who did not take these heritage sites forward during their time, but even now they refuse to stop. They make irresponsible statements and even comment on boatmen. Before 2014, their steamers ran on diesel and kerosene. Now CNG has been introduced and their income has increased. To divert attention from all this, as soon as new work begins, these people start spreading misleading propaganda. See few pics of dismantling of parts of Manikarnika Ghats

title: Woman thief bites off ₹4.5 lakh chain in Jhansi:Incident caught on CCTV at Bhagwat Katha, 4 women lose jewellery amid stage crowd chaos
summary: A female thief cut a chain worth 4.5 lakhs with her teeth in Jhansi. During the Bhagwat Katha, as soon as there was pushing near the stage, the female thief approached the retired inspector's wife. She surrounded them with her friend. One placed her hand on the woman's shoulder. The other pressed her mouth to the neck and stole the chain by cutting it with her teeth. The incident was executed in just 10 seconds. During this time, BJP MLA Ravi Sharma had also come to listen to the katha. The incident occurred in Ayodhyapuri Colony of Sipri Bazar police station area on January 14, but the video emerged today. The two female thieves have not been identified yet. See 3 pictures of the woman's chain theft- Ayodhyapuri Colony resident Dayashankar Vyas said, 'I am a retired inspector. My wife, Gyan Devi, is a member of the Satsang Sunderkand Committee. A Bhagwat Katha is being organized in the colony. My wife used to go daily to listen to the katha. On January 14, BJP MLA Ravi Sharma and his wife were going to honor my wife. Wife came to the katha with daughter-in-law and children. Here, fruits, flowers, and toys were being distributed from the stage during Krishna's birth celebration. Many women reached the stage of receiving these. This led to pushing and shoving. At that time, two female thieves surrounded my wife and snatched her chain.' One placed hand on shoulder, other committed theft Dayashankar further said, 'One female thief put her hand on my wife's shoulder, and the other woman cut and stole the gold chain with her teeth. Both disappeared with the chain. Later, when the daughter-in-law and son saw, then we came to know. The chain was 35 grams. Its value is approximately Rs 4.5 lakhs.' That day, four women's chains were stolen. There was no police arrangement on the day of the incident, but the police were deployed after the MLA's reprimand. We have submitted an application to the police station demanding action. Both female thieves can be seen in the video.'

title: Doctors not found in 45 Agra hospitals:License suspended, paramedical staff and fire safety equipment found lacking during verification
summary: The Health Department has taken a strict stance on the negligence of medical standards related to patient safety in Agra. License renewals have been suspended for 45 private hospitals due to deficiencies found in essential standards such as deployment of specialist doctors in ICU, trained paramedical staff, medical waste management, and fire safety. Hospital operators have been issued notices with instructions to rectify the shortcomings within a week. A total of 1317 medical institutions are registered with the Health Department. These include 537 hospitals, 513 clinics, 149 pathology labs, and 108 diagnostic centers. The department is renewing licenses based on physical verification of institutions according to 17 prescribed medical standards. During inspection, 45 hospitals were found to have incomplete standards, while complaints of negligence in treatment have also emerged against 27 hospitals. During physical verification, the health department team found several serious deficiencies. Many hospitals did not have specialist doctors deployed in ICUs for 24 hours. There was also a shortage of trained paramedical staff. Life-saving equipment was found incomplete, and fire safety equipment was non-functional at many places. Some hospitals did not even have a fire NOC. Negligence was also found in medical waste management. Biomedical waste was not being collected and disposed of according to standards. Additionally, CCTV cameras were not installed at the doctors' chambers and entrance gates. Information boards at many hospitals did not display details like doctors' names, fee details, affidavits of serving physicians, and records of admitted and discharged patients. Playing with Patients' lives Health department officials say that ignoring medical standards directly puts patients' lives at risk. The presence of a specialist in the ICU is mandatory 24 hours. Due to the absence of specialist doctors for surgeries other than cesarean, serious patients often lose their lives. Without systems like CCTV, it becomes difficult to identify the responsible doctor. CMO's Statement CMO Dr. Arun Srivastava said that medical standards were found incomplete in 45 hospitals. Affidavits of doctors providing services in these hospitals were also not found. Notices have been issued to fulfill necessary standards, including ICU, medical waste management, and other requirements. Verification will be done again after the fixed time. If facilities are not found complete, licenses of the concerned hospitals will be suspended. IMA's Position IMA President Dr. Pankaj Nagaich said that the organization has directed all its members to mandatorily fulfill medical standards in hospitals. A meeting has also been held with health department officials on this issue. Most of the hospitals that do not meet the standards are run by non-medical operators. This information has also been given to the CMO.

title: From Charan Singh’s protégé to Samajwadi founder leader:Mulayam’s journey shows ambition, risk-taking and survival skills in decades of shifting alliances and power struggles
summary: The soil of Uttar Pradesh has produced not just crops, but also iron-willed leaders. One such name is Mulayam Singh Yadav. His father's teaching was - 'If you can't fly, then run, if you can't run, then walk, if you can't walk, then crawl, but don't stop.' Mulayam did politics this way. He rose from opposing Congress, but joined hands with them several times when needed. He fought against the Ram Mandir movement, then later stood with its leader, Kalyan Singh. He emerged from Chaudhary Charan Singh's legacy, but became Chief Minister by opposing his son Ajit Singh. In Dainik Bhaskar's series Political Arena, the story of a leader who was called 'Little Napoleon'. Who remained the flag bearer of experimentalism in politics and stayed relevant in every era due to political maneuvering... Year 1980, Saifai village of Etawah The Congress flag had already waved at Jaswantnagar's political gathering. Mulayam Singh had lost the election. Congress's Balram Singh Yadav had defeated him. Mulayam had already gone to the assembly three times from this seat. This was the reason they were quite disappointed with this defeat and were sitting with some colleagues in the election office. He suddenly got up and said, "See you tomorrow." A colleague said, "What's done is done. Sit for a while, then everyone will leave." Mulayam didn't say anything, just got up and left. He reached home and went straight to his room and lay down on the cot. His only sister, Kamla, saw him coming but didn't say anything. Everyone at home was sad. Khichdi was made for dinner. After a while, Kamla went to Mulayam's room with food. There were tears in Mulayam's eyes. Standing at the door of the room, Kamla spoke up- "Is life over?" Mulayam said with a choked voice- "Chaudhary Sahab had so much faith in me... Hope he doesn't break down from this defeat." Kamla said, "Something good must be written. Don't try to win just Jaswantnagar, try to win the country. You'll win here automatically." Mulayam Singh’s political rise gained momentum when Chaudhary Charan Singh appointed him state president of the Lok Dal, a moment that filled his family with joy. At the same time, Congress made VP Singh the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, where the fear of dacoits was widespread. VP Singh launched aggressive police encounters to project a tough image, but Mulayam opposed this approach, arguing that Dalits and backward classes were being harassed in the name of law and order. Mulayam raised the issue with Charan Singh and later mobilised leaders like George Fernandes and Karpoori Thakur to build opposition against VP Singh’s policies. The movement created strong anti-Congress sentiment among backward classes, forcing VP Singh to resign and strengthening Mulayam’s image in UP. National politics soon shifted dramatically with Indira Gandhi’s assassination, the anti-Sikh riots, and Rajiv Gandhi becoming Prime Minister. Though VP Singh joined Rajiv’s cabinet as Finance Minister, the Bofors controversy split the Congress, bringing former rivals VP Singh and Mulayam together. On October 11, 1988, several socialist parties merged to form the Janata Dal. VP Singh became the National president, while Mulayam emerged as UP president. With simultaneous national and state elections approaching, Mulayam had become the key political force in UP and the most influential backward-class leader after Charan Singh’s death. One day, Rajiv Gandhi called the then Congress state president, Balram Singh Yadav, to Delhi. Rajiv said, "Mulayam Singh must be stopped by any means." Balram said, "When I had defeated him, I didn't expect he would become so big." Rajiv Gandhi- "What should be the strategy? If we don't stop him, we will lose." Balram Yadav- "His hold among the backwards has increased. Ajit Singh is still inexperienced, and Mulayam is taking Charan Singh's place. We will have to play the backward card." As per the decision taken in the meeting, to counter Mulayam Singh Yadav, the 'Yadav Trio' - Balram Yadav, Chandrajeet Yadav, and Ramnaresh Yadav were fielded. Chandrajeet was close to Indira and Sanjay Gandhi. Ramnaresh Yadav was UP CM during the Janata Party time. He had joined Janata Dal but was unhappy with Mulayam Singh becoming the state president, and came to Congress. Still, Congress's strategy didn't work. A slogan started echoing across the state- "Thakur's wisdom, Ahir's strength, this is what Janata Dal is named." Mulayam's stature grew even more. Congress faced heavy defeats in both the UP Assembly and the Lok Sabha. VP Singh became PM, but he had a grudge against Mulayam. He didn't want Mulayam to become CM. He wanted to make Ajit Singh, son of former Prime Minister Chaudhary Charan Singh, the CM. December, 1989. Tilak Hall, Lucknow. A meeting of Janata Dal MLAs was underway. The name for CM was to be finalized. Inside and outside the hall, supporters of Ajit and Mulayam were raising slogans. Then Mulayam stood up and said - "Be quiet..." The sloganeering increased - "Name is Mulayam, work is like steel." Mulayam said again - "Listen to me. Be quiet. There will be opportunities for slogans." The sloganeering stopped. Two observers from Delhi, Madhu Dandavate and Surendra Mohan, were also present there. Madhu had a slip in his pocket, on which VP Singh had endorsed Ajit Singh for CM. Madhu stood up and put his hand in his pocket. Mulayam became suspicious. He also stood up and said loudly- "Wait, wait..." Whispers started in the hall. Mulayam said, "Don't take out the slip. You have come here to conduct fair elections. Just do that." When the election happened, most MLAs supported Mulayam Singh. This is how Mulayam Singh Yadav became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh for the first time. January 1, 1990 The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court ordered mapping photography and a structural survey of the disputed land in Ayodhya. Both the Center and State had Janata Dal governments. BJP was supporting both governments from outside. Despite this, through the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, they had made life difficult for the government. The country's politics were changing. Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP), Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), and BJP started raising the Ram temple issue at every corner and intersection. Mulayam Singh was worried. He went to Delhi to meet VP Singh - "Prime Minister, BJP people are fueling communal politics. The mosque siege could begin anytime. Why don't you talk to them?" VP Singh didn't give much reaction. Just said - "Okay, I will talk." August 7, 1990 Prime Minister VP Singh implemented the Mandal Commission recommendations. 27% reservation was provided for backward classes. Mulayam held a meeting with his people in the state. Someone said- "VP Singh will become the god of backwards. We will be left behind." Mulayam said, "Nothing will happen. I have a move." Everyone fell silent. Everyone knew Netaji would make such a move that would destroy everyone's plans. Mulayam said, "We will implement reservation at the panchayat level." Mulayam became the first chief minister in the country to do this. This further strengthened Mulayam's image among backward castes. Meanwhile, the BJP was restless. The Mandal move had turned everything upside down. A large part of the country started mobilizing towards the opposition. On the other hand, violent fires against the reservation erupted across the country. August 8, 1990, Patna A Janata Dal rally was underway. Mulayam Singh Yadav was accompanied by Lalu Yadav and Sharad Yadav. After securing the backwards, now it was time to win the trust of minorities. Mulayam Singh thundered- "If one Muslim's life is threatened, a hundred Yadavs will be ready to give their lives." BJP became restless. The whole country was stuck in the politics of 'Mandal and Kamandal'. On August 13, BJP President LK Advani held a meeting with Muslim leaders. He proposed, "If Muslims withdraw their claim from Ram Janmabhoomi, we won't press our demands for Mathura and Varanasi." Muslim leaders rejected this offer. Advani started the Rath Yatra from Somnath Temple, Gujarat, on September 25, 1990. The Rath Yatra was receiving tremendous support. Mulayam held another meeting with his associates - "The atmosphere is building in BJP's favor. Muslims are scared. Muslim leaders are pressuring me to do something." Someone said, "If the chariot reaches Ayodhya, something terrible will happen." Mulayam - "What if I don't let the chariot enter UP?" Silence fell in the meeting. One person said - "How will this happen...?" Mulayam said, "I will arrest Advani." And the meeting ended with this decision. VP knew that if Mulayam stopped the Rath Yatra, minorities would also stand behind him. Backward castes were already in Mulayam's favor. To counter this, VP called Bihar CM Lalu Yadav and said- "Stop the Rath Yatra in Bihar. Arrest Advani." Lalu Yadav got Advani arrested in Samastipur, Bihar, on October 23. Sporadic violence occurred in many places. Curfew was also imposed in areas around Ayodhya. Mulayam also got many VHP leaders arrested. Mulayam Singh began to be portrayed as a villain across the country. BJP pressured VP Singh to make Mulayam release VHP leaders. VP Singh sent his close associate, Farrukhabad MP Santosh Bharatiya, to Lucknow to convince Mulayam. Mulayam Singh became angry. He said in an angry tone, "I cannot release them." Santosh was expecting such a response. He threatened Mulayam - "If you don't release them, the BJP will withdraw support. The government will fall." Mulayam said, "I am not worried about that." October 28, 1990 National and international media were in Lucknow. Time magazine's journalist Robert Nickelsberg asked Mulayam, "What will you do to save the mosque?" Mulayam said, "Whether the government survives or not, the mosque will fall only over my dead body." The journalist fired a second question- "Is Ram not a matter of faith for you?" Mulayam replied- "I believe in the Ram who considers everyone equal. I believe in the Ram that Gandhi believed in." Just then, another journalist said, "Advani is coming to Ayodhya." Mulayam smiled and said, "He has never come to Ayodhya till today. Why has he suddenly developed a love for Ayodhya? If he comes, we'll see." October 30, 1990 There were about 10 barricades along the 126-kilometer route on the Lucknow-Faizabad Road. Early in the morning, crowds of thousands of kar sevaks were moving towards the Babri Masjid. Seeing the huge crowd, security forces started sweating. Phones started ringing in Mulayam Singh's office- "The crowd is growing. The situation is getting out of control." In no time, some kar sevaks climbed the mosque's dome and started waving saffron flags. It was afternoon. Suddenly, the police opened fire. Within moments, the field filled with thousands of people emptied, but the scene ahead was horrific. Blood splattered everywhere... A similar scene appeared again on November 2. According to government figures, 16 kar sevaks were killed in police firing over two days. As a result, the BJP withdrew support. VP Singh's government at the center fell. Socialist leader Chandra Shekhar broke away from the Janata Dal and formed the Samajwadi Janata Party with 64 MPs. Mulayam Singh Yadav joined him and remained Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister with Congress support, even though he had earlier opposed the Congress. When Congress withdrew support, both the central and UP governments fell, leading to fresh elections. During this period, the BJP rose sharply by pushing the Ram temple issue, damaging Mulayam’s image and branding him as anti-Hindu. Even in his home district, Etawah, public sentiment turned against him. In the 1991 elections, the BJP won 221 seats and formed the government in UP under Kalyan Singh. Facing political isolation and declining influence, Mulayam realised the need to rebuild his base independently. His faith in Chandra Shekhar weakened, and in October 1992, he announced the formation of the Samajwadi Party in Lucknow. Soon after, the Babri Masjid demolition triggered riots across UP. The Kalyan Singh government was dismissed, President’s Rule was imposed, and mid-term elections were announced. In this changing political climate, BSP leader Kanshi Ram described Mulayam as secular and pro-Dalit. For the 1993 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party (SP) and BSP formed an alliance and came to power. However, the alliance broke in 1995, leading to the fall of the government. Mulayam Singh Yadav then shifted his focus to national politics and won the 1996 Lok Sabha election from Mainpuri. At the Centre, non-Congress and non-BJP parties formed the United Front, of which SP was a part. Mulayam was a strong contender for the Prime Minister’s post, but internal opposition from leaders like Lalu Yadav and Sharad Yadav blocked his rise. During this period, Mulayam grew close to Amar Singh, who became his key political strategist. Amar Singh advised Mulayam to broaden his social base and keep channels open with the Congress. Their partnership strengthened SP, and Amar Singh rose quickly within the party. In 2002, SP emerged as the largest party in the UP Assembly with 143 seats but lacked a majority. Through Amar Singh’s political negotiations, Congress extended outside support, and several BSP MLAs backed SP. Even former rival Kalyan Singh supported Mulayam. With this support, Mulayam Singh Yadav became Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh for the third time. Year 2007-08 As allegations grew against Mulayam Singh Yadav, the Samajwadi Party began losing backward class votes to the BSP and faced criticism as a party of strongmen. Mulayam sought advice from Amar Singh, who warned that SP was losing support among backward classes, Muslims, and farmers, and suggested making a bold political move. Mulayam then met Kalyan Singh, a former BJP leader sidelined by his party. They decided to work together to counter the BJP in Uttar Pradesh. However, this alliance proved costly. Muslims grew angry, the Congress attacked SP, and Mayawati called the move a betrayal of secularism. The strategy backfired badly in the 2007 elections, leading to SP’s defeat. After the loss, Mulayam publicly admitted that allying with a leader linked to the Babri Masjid demolition was a serious mistake and apologised to his party. Despite criticism and failed experiments, Mulayam remained a central figure in Indian politics. He served three times as UP Chief Minister, once as Defence Minister, was elected MP seven times and MLA ten times, and came close to becoming Prime Minister twice. *** Reference Creative liberty has been used to make the story interesting.

title: 4 friends from UP survive deadly snowstorm:Car fell into valley, minus 25°C cold, 36-hour survival fight ended with cops rescue; read their sagacious story
summary: -25 °C temperature...there was snow everywhere. No one else was visible there except us. We called out, honked the car horn, banged utensils, shouted and screamed, but there was no one there to hear us. On January 12th, during daytime, a helicopter passed over us. We showed a red cloth, waved our hands, and even called out, but the people in the helicopter didn't see us. This is what Shivam Chaudhary, who returned from Leh, has to say. Due to Google Maps, 4 friends from Agra who lost their way fought a 36-hour battle for survival in the snowfall. The last 3 hours of this were particularly terrifying. They say that at one point, it felt like they wouldn't survive. Tears were flowing from their eyes as they remembered their families. After much struggle, they managed to return home alive. Dainik Bhaskar spoke with Shivam Chaudhary and Yash Mittal. Learned about their story of 2 nights and 3 days spent in terror. Read the report... Car slipped in snow, fell 20 feet down into valley Four friends met at Shivam’s house and left for Leh by car on January 9. After staying in Pang on January 10, they headed towards Manali on January 11. Near Nakila, around 2:30 am, the car skidded on the snow and fell about 20 feet into a valley. With no help in sight, they spent the night inside the car using the heater to survive the freezing cold. Even after daylight, no one was visible nearby, and extreme cold forced them back into the car. They remained trapped for nearly 36 hours. Eventually, the diesel ran out, the heater stopped, there was no food, phones shut down, and all four began to suffer serious effects of the cold. Then we decided that instead of staying here, it's better to fight for life. Because if we remain stuck here, survival would be difficult. Due to the blocked road, no one would come here, nor would anyone hear our voice. Then we planned that we had no choice but to walk on foot. After walking 20 km, around 12:30 PM on January 13, we saw an abandoned factory near Whiskey Nala. We spent the night there. We were inside when we heard some people outside. When we looked outside, we found that they were police officers who had arrived there searching for us. Now it felt like our lives would be saved. Seeing them brought tears to our eyes. It felt like God had sent angels to help us. We hugged them and started crying. Shivam explained - The closed factory where we stayed was a little off the road. There was a signboard outside. We wrote 'Help Us' on it. After this, we came into the factory and tried to protect ourselves from the cold. Sudhanshu was unwell, so he had gone to sleep. Seeing our message on the roadside signboard, Neuma police station officers arrived at the scene in the afternoon. As soon as we heard the jeep's sound, I, Jayveer and Yash ran outside. Our hearts were overwhelmed seeing the police officers in front of us. Tears welled up in our eyes. Had video call with family, then lost contact The families of all four reached Leh searching for them. Yash, Shivam and Sudhansu arrived in Agra on Thursday night, while Jayveer arrived on Friday evening. Their car is still in Leh. It couldn't come due to road blockage. After reaching Ladakh, Shivam and his friends got a new mobile number. Then they stayed continuously connected with family, and conversations continued. On January 9, everyone was at Pangong Lake in Leh. From there, they also talked to home via video call. Since then, their contact was lost. Family members tried to contact the same number many times but could not get through. Worried, the family filed a missing person complaint at Sadar Police Station on January 11. Car location found through satellite Shivam Chaudhary, Jayveer Singh, Yash Mittal and Sudhanshu Fojdar went from Agra to Gulmarg. From there, they reached Pangong Lake via Sonamarg. On January 9th, around 5:30 PM, all four made a video call to show their families the scenery there. After this, contact with them was lost. Shivam's father, Daulatram, says - We all got worried when there was no information for 2 days. I contacted the local police as well as the local MP and other public representatives. After that, help was sought from the Defence and Home Ministries. The army also became active upon receiving the information. The youth's vehicle was located via satellite. The vehicle was in Pang, about 125 kilometres from Leh, near the Manali route. Then the army and police reached these young men. Now know what happened between January 9 to 13... January 9: At 5 PM, all four youths talked to their families. After this, they left for Leh. There, they saw the Manali board near Kharu. They started walking on that route. January 10: Stopped at Pang itself. January 11: Left for Manali. The road ahead was closed. After going ahead from Sarchu, we had to return. Near Nakila, around 2:30 at night, the car slipped on the snow and got stuck in a 20-foot deep ditch. Spent the night in the car with the heater on amidst the snow. January 12: The next day was also spent relying on the heater. After the car's diesel ran out, the heater - our only support - also stopped working. Then planned to walk on foot. January 13: At around 12:30 in the afternoon, after walking about 20 kilometres, reached a closed factory near Whisky Nala. Spent the entire night there. Meanwhile, Ladakh Police also reached there while searching for them. Everyone was rescued and brought back to Leh.

title: Worst fog of the season in UP, 40 vehicles collide:5 dead, including an 18-month-old girl, 100 trains delayed; schools closed in 9 cities
summary: Uttar Pradesh is reeling under a double spell of severe cold and cold wave conditions, with the state witnessing the densest fog of the season on Saturday. Dense fog was reported from 53 districts, including Lucknow and Kanpur, since morning, reducing visibility to near zero at several places. The fog severely disrupted road, rail, and air traffic across the state. In many areas, visibility dropped to such low levels that commuters struggled to see even a few metres ahead. Icy winds added to the chill, forcing people travelling in vehicles to cover their hands and faces, while bonfires were seen across residential areas. According to official data, Azamgarh, Kanpur, Ayodhya, and Hardoi were the coldest districts in the past 24 hours, recording a minimum temperature of 4 degrees Celsius. In view of the prevailing cold wave, district administrations in Noida, Greater Noida, Saharanpur, Badaun, and Sambhal have ordered the closure of schools up to Class 8. Train services were hit hard, with over 50 trains on the Gorakhpur–Lucknow–Prayagraj route running late by one to ten hours. Even premium services, including Vande Bharat and Shatabdi Express trains, failed to maintain schedules. Flight operations were also affected, with passengers reporting long delays at airports. The India Meteorological Department said snowfall in the higher reaches has led to a sharp drop in temperatures across Uttar Pradesh. Most districts are currently under a ‘cold day’ alert, and cold wave conditions are likely to continue for the next four to five days. Now the weather pictures- Why did the weather take a sudden turn? According to the India Meteorological Department, a powerful jet stream is currently active over west–north India, leading to a sharp change in weather conditions across Uttar Pradesh. Meteorologists said jet stream winds — fast-flowing air currents that move like a river in the upper atmosphere are blowing at a speed of around 232 kmph at an altitude of 12.6 km above mean sea level. The impact of these high-speed winds is being felt at lower levels, resulting in intensified cold conditions, dense fog, and strong surface winds in the plains, including UP. In addition, recent snowfall in the higher reaches has further strengthened cold northerly winds, pushing temperatures down across the state. Weather outlook for the next two days January 18: Light rain or drizzle is likely at isolated places in western Uttar Pradesh. Cold winds are expected to continue, increasing the chill factor across most districts. January 19: Drizzle may persist in parts of western UP, while cloud cover is likely to increase over several districts in eastern UP. Cold winds will remain active, keeping day temperatures low. The Meteorological Department has warned that cold day conditions may continue in many districts over the next few days.

title: Meerut murder case reveals Paras and Ruby love story:Lawyer says, 'couple wanted marriage, fled home, while accused insists he did not kill mother'
summary: The truth of Paras-Ruby's love story has come to light in the Meerut Sunita murder case. Paras Som, accused of Sunita's murder, is in jail. On January 15, Paras's lawyer went to meet him in the district jail with his uncle. For 1 hour, they discussed the entire sequence of events with Paras alone around 3 points. First- How did the love story with Ruby begin, and why did it come to running away? Second- If they were running away from home, how did Sunita die? Third- If Ruby loves him, why is she giving statements against Paras now? After returning from the district jail, Dainik Bhaskar team understood the complete love story from Paras's lawyer, Balram Som. Read the report... Read the conversation from the jail meeting room... We studied together in school; she was in 12th, and I was a 9th-grade student Paras was introduced to the lawyer in the district jail's meeting room. The lawyer asked - When did you first meet Ruby? Recalling, Paras explained, Ruby and I both studied at the village's Janta Inter College. We first saw each other in college. Since we were in the same school, we would often run into each other. Once I was going to drink water, Ruby was coming from the front. She smiled when she saw me, so I smiled back. She was studying in 12th grade, and I was a 9th-grade student. There was nothing like love at that time. Normal conversations would happen, I would ask about her studies, and she would talk about me. After leaving school, we started talking on mobile The lawyer asked - Then when did love happen? Paras started narrating the story further - We were from the same village, studying in the same school. My house was also just 1km away from her house. That's why we started meeting while coming and going in the village. About 3 years ago, we met at a village wedding. Ruby was also there. We both smiled at each other. From that day, a new story of our friendship began. We would meet daily at school and talk. Our conversations kept growing, and we didn't even realize when we started liking each other. We met daily at school. Spent a lot of time together. Had lunch together too. All the kids at our school would often tease us. They all knew that our friendship was of a different type. That's when we decided that we would stay together for life. Ruby is older than me. After passing 12th grade, she went to college for graduation. After leaving school, we started having difficulty meeting. But we would talk on the phone. Ruby also had a mobile phone. Sometimes she would call me, sometimes I would call her. We have sent many messages to each other. I have saved those messages too. When needed, I will show those messages in court. We would talk for long hours on the phone. Paras said - Ruby was troubled by the marriage being fixed In 2024, our families found out about our affair. Not just them... the whole village came to know about it. Then there was a fight between our families. Ruby's family said about me that I had misled their daughter. My family was angry, and they took away my mobile. It became difficult for us to meet. Then I would often talk to Ruby from my mother's phone. Sometimes we would also talk through friends' phones. But then Ruby would be the one calling me. Then one day, I found out that Ruby's family had arranged her marriage; she was very worried while talking on the phone. She said that she would only marry me and did not want to marry anyone else. Ruby told her family - I won't marry anywhere else I learned from my friends that Ruby had told her parents that she would not marry anyone except me. Her family members were quite angry about this. They said that wherever we go, you will have to marry there. Ruby said that if they force her to marry, she will run away from home. She had told me on the phone that my family won't let me marry you, so we will have to run away from home. She used to send me love letters, too Ruby has written me many letters. When we couldn't talk on mobile, Ruby would send me letters with help from two village friends. Both those girls knew me, too. This way, we started communicating through letters as well. Through those letters, we would sometimes meet up. I still want to marry Ruby Lawyer Balram told us - After reaching jail, Paras would keep asking about Ruby in between telling his story. We told him that Ruby was not feeling well. Then he asked if we could arrange a conversation with his Ruby. Then we told him that it was not possible to arrange the conversation. He told the lawyer - I still want to marry Ruby today. If possible, please arrange my marriage with Ruby. Because when we were coming back home, Ruby had said that her family members won't leave me now. I will be kept as a hostage in the house, and later will be forcefully married. Paras told his lawyer, Balram Som - I have kept many records of conversations between Ruby and me. I have saved those messages and chats. Which will reveal our truth in front of the court. He also said that he has some photos of him and Ruby together, in which they are together. Paras's mobile was taken away after compromise in the panchayat The lawyer also says that Paras did not have a mobile for the last 3 months. In 2024, after the dispute between Paras-Ruby's families was settled in a compromise a few days later, Paras's family members took away his mobile phone. Due to not having a phone, Paras was unable to communicate with Ruby. Then Paras would secretly talk to Ruby from his mother's phone. Ruby would also call Paras. These details will also be included in their case. What happened on the day of murder? Paras said - I did not kill her mother When the lawyer asked Paras what happened on the day of the murder? Then Paras couldn't say much. He only said that I did not commit the murder... I am innocent. He also said that I did not kidnap Ruby. Ruby came with me on her own will. Ruby had also planned the escape. I had thought about where we would go, what we would do. I hadn't thought so much would happen. Ruby had said that her family was arranging her marriage somewhere else, which she didn't want to do, so let's run away from home. Paras said - After running away from Kapsad, we jumped into a canal (small channel). My shoe got washed away in the water. I became barefoot. Then Ruby gave me her shoes. She said - You wear these. She kept walking barefoot with me. Then, moving ahead, we took a lift from a truck driver. Sitting in that truck, we reached Saharanpur. That truck driver gave a slipper, which Ruby wore. When Ruby and I were caught, Paras was still wearing Ruby's shoes. After running away from Meerut, we didn't stay anywhere for long; we just kept moving around while traveling by train, so that the police couldn't trace us. Paras said - I don't understand why she is lying The lawyer said that Paras is not in a condition to reveal much right now. He is stressed and sad. He kept saying that Ruby cannot lie. We both love each other very much. We have had a relationship for 3 years. We want to live together. Paras is unable to tell much about the murder and murder weapon. Right now, Paras is also anxious and troubled. Now we will gradually arrange his meetings with his family members. When he becomes normal, we will get more information from him, and evidence related to Ruby-Paras's conversations and relationship will also be found.

title: Bajaj Finance manager found dead at Hyatt Regency in Lucknow:Had flown in from Mumbai for meeting, alcohol bottles found in room
summary: A senior manager of Bajaj Finance was found unconscious in his hotel room at a five-star hotel in Lucknow on Friday morning and later declared dead at a government hospital, police said. The deceased has been identified as Mohammad Fahimuddin (47), a resident of Thane district in Maharashtra. He had travelled from Mumbai to Lucknow to attend an official meeting and was staying at Hyatt Regency Lucknow. Colleagues raised alarm after calls went unanswered According to police, Fahimuddin was scheduled to attend a meeting with the Bajaj Finance team on Friday morning. Around 8 am, his colleagues tried calling him several times, but there was no response. When the calls remained unanswered till around 9.30 am, a few team members went to the hotel and informed the reception that Fahimuddin was not responding. Door locked from inside, staff alerted reception Hotel staff sent a service worker to check the room. The door was locked from inside and did not open despite repeated knocks. The worker then looked through a side window and saw Fahimuddin lying unconscious on the bed. The matter was immediately reported to the hotel reception. The door was opened using a master key in the presence of staff. Police said his pulse was still present at the time. He was taken to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences in a 108 ambulance, where doctors declared him dead. The body has been kept in the hospital mortuary for post-mortem. Alcohol bottles, cigarette packets found in room ACP Vinay Dwivedi said alcohol bottles and several cigarette packets were recovered from the hotel room. “Prima facie, his health condition appears to have deteriorated due to excessive consumption of alcohol and smoking. Other angles are also being investigated,” the officer said. Police said the post-mortem examination will be conducted after the arrival of the deceased’s wife, who has left Mumbai for Lucknow. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report.

title: Brijbhushan Singh prepares to contest election from Faizabad:Vinay Katiyar already active; will BJP give ticket to Bahubali?
summary: After Rashtra Katha in Gonda, these two questions are being discussed in UP's political corridors. Former MP from Kaiserganj and strongman Brijbhushan Singh has started preparations to contest elections. Meanwhile, BJP's firebrand leader Vinay Katiyar has become active in Ayodhya after a long time. In a special conversation with Bhaskar, Katiyar said, " We will contest assembly elections first, then Lok Sabha elections. In such a situation, will the BJP hand over the Ayodhya seat, considered a symbol of Hindutva and nationalism, to Brijbhushan Sharan Singh? To know the answers to all these questions, read... The case of sexual harassment of women wrestlers is still ongoing BJP did not give a ticket in 2024 to Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, who was a six-time MP from Gonda, Balrampur and Kaiserganj, and was accused of sexual harassment of women wrestlers. In his place, his younger son Karan Bhushan Sharan Singh was fielded in the election from Kaiserganj. Karan Bhushan is currently an MP from Kaiserganj. In the sexual harassment case, Brij Bhushan has been acquitted under the POCSO Act section, but the sexual harassment case is still under consideration. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh organised a grand Rashtrakatha in his Nandani Niketanam this month. Many personalities from the political, film, sports and social world participated in Rashtrakatha. Brij Bhushan recently gave an emotional statement- There was a conspiracy against me, I was removed as part of a plot. If I remain alive till 2029, I will definitely go to Parliament once with full respect. Brij Bhushan Singh's MP son Karan Bhushan announced that in 2029, both he and his father will go to Parliament. Supporting this, Brij Bhushan said - 'Both will contest Lok Sabha elections, if BJP gives a ticket, then good, otherwise will contest from somewhere else.' After this statement by Brij Bhushan, discussions have started in political corridors that Brij Bhushan will field his son Karan Bhushan from his Kaiserganj seat, while he himself will contest from the Faizabad seat. Want to know why Brij Bhushan wants Faizabad seat? Even after the construction of the grand temple at Sri Ram Janmabhoomi and the Pran Pratishtha ceremony, BJP's Lallu Singh lost the election from Faizabad in 2024. This is why Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh is looking for political possibilities there. He and his close associates believe that the BJP will be looking for a strong alternative to Lallu Singh in 2029. In such a situation, Brij Bhushan could become the party's choice. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh studied at Saket College in Ayodhya. He also served as the general secretary of the student union in the college. However, he went across the Saryu to Gonda to contest the assembly and Lok Sabha elections. Hoardings put up in Ayodhya during Rashtrakatha During the Rashtrakatha, Brij Bhushan and his supporters put up a large number of hoardings and banners in Ayodhya. His supporters also privately believe that if given the opportunity, Netaji could try his luck from the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat. Brij Bhushan himself has said that, keeping in mind the insistence of supporters, he may contest the election. Vinay Katiyar big challenge before Brij Bhushan Political analysts believe that in Ayodhya, bigger than Lallu Singh, BJP's fiery leader Vinay Katiyar is the major obstacle in Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh's path. After meeting with BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary, Katiyar has openly declared that Faizabad is his seat and he will contest from that seat only. Faizabad, Ambedkar Nagar and nearby seats have a large number of Kurmi voters. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP did not get the Kurmi vote, resulting in defeats in Ayodhya and surrounding seats. Learning from 2024, the BJP has devised a strategy to cultivate the Kurmi vote bank for 2027 and then 2029. Vinay Katiyar's active involvement in politics is also part of that strategy. If Vinay Katiyar announces his candidature for the Lok Sabha elections, it will be difficult for Brijbhushan to get a chance from Ayodhya due to caste equations. In terms of caste equations, handing over Faizabad to Brijbhushan will not be beneficial for the BJP. Brij Bhushan is playing pressure politics Political analysts believe that Brij Bhushan and his son have adopted a pressure strategy by announcing their intention to contest elections in 2029. After Gonda MP Kirtiwardhan Singh became a minister at the centre, his political stature and influence in the region have become greater than Brij Bhushan's. Meanwhile, he also has an ongoing political rivalry with CM Yogi Adityanath. In such a situation, to ensure there are no obstacles for his family's politics in 2027 and 2029, he is creating pressure through statements from now itself. So, whether he gets a new seat or not, at least the current legacy remains intact. Take a look at the political history of Faizabad After independence, Congress started its winning streak in Faizabad in the 1957 general elections. So far, 17 Lok Sabha elections have been held on the Faizabad seat, out of which Congress has won 7 times. SP won four times, while BJP won five times, and CPI won once. In this way, after the Emergency, no single political party has dominated Faizabad. The people of Faizabad have chosen their MP according to the time, circumstances and caste equations. Senior journalist Triyug Narayan Tiwari believes that Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has an old connection with Faizabad. He studied at Saket College and started student politics from there. He learned wrestling at Hanumangarhi. His and his supporters' gestures indicate that Brij Bhushan wants to contest the upcoming Lok Sabha elections from Faizabad. He is also quite active among the saints and sages here, participating in religious programs and supporting them. But the Ayodhya ticket is decided by the RSS. RSS would want its own cadre to contest the election. In such a situation, it will be difficult for Brijbhushan to get a ticket from Ayodhya. Due to PDA, SP will also not consider it appropriate to cut Awadesh Prasad's ticket and give it to Brijbhushan. Moreover, it will be difficult for Brijbhushan to win by contesting as an independent.

title: Fresh currency notes sold openly on Kanpur roads:Bank staff accused of diverting wedding season cash bundles to black market for huge profits
summary: 'A bundle of 100 fresh (new) 10 rupee notes will cost 1370 rupees... 20 rupee bundle is more expensive... it will cost 2480 rupees... 100 notes of 1 rupee bundle costs 2700 rupees... need 10 lakhs... need 5 lakhs... just make the payment... will give right now... You won't get new note bundles in the bank... bank officers deliver here... we buy from them by paying extra money...' The fresh notes that you should get from banks are being sold on UP roads after going black from the bank. The centre point is Kanpur's Ghantaghar area. Here, a bundle of 100 fresh 1-rupee notes is being sold for 2,700 rupees. This means for 1 US dollar, you will get only 3 fresh 1 rupee notes and 35 paise, while the dollar is worth 90 rupees. Similarly, fresh notes of 5, 10, and 20 rupees are being sold with extra charges. Actually, the wedding season has begun. In such a situation, the demand for crisp notes for the groom's garlands and other rituals has increased. When common people go to banks for fresh notes, they don't get them. Bank staff turn them away, saying there are no new notes. While the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) has strict orders that banks cannot refuse if fresh notes are available. How did fresh notes from RBI to banks end up being sold in the market? To find the answer to this question, Dainik Bhaskar's team conducted an investigation in Kanpur. Read the full revelation... Are there fresh notes in the market? Our investigation started with this question. We reached Shastri Nagar in Kanpur. Here, fresh notes are strung into garlands and sold. We met Ruby. She told us that if we take bundles of fresh notes from her, an extra charge of Rs 500 will be taken, because she also buys fresh notes at higher prices from shops in the Ghanta Ghar area. Reporter: Want to get a garland of notes made...? Ruby: Which one... 10 rupee or 20 rupee...? Reporter: How much will it cost for 10 rupee notes...? Ruby: Will you provide the bundle of notes... or do we need to arrange from our side...? Reporter: Tell me both options... Ruby: One garland uses 500 rupees worth of 10 rupee notes... how many notes do you want to use...? Reporter: Let's say... if we use a bundle of 1000 rupees (100 new notes) of 10 rupee notes then...? Ruby: If you provide the bundle, we'll charge 300 rupees for making it... Reporter: How much will it cost for two bundles...? Ruby: Then the total will be 1800 rupees... Reporter: Meaning... why so much... bundle of 1000 rupees... and 300 rupees charge... that's 1300 rupees... then why 1800 rupees...? Ruby: 500 rupees will be charged for fresh notes... Ruby's statement made it clear that an extra charge is taken in the name of fresh notes. Now we needed to find out where these new notes were being sold. To get this answer, we continued the conversation. They bring bundles of fresh notes bought in black market Reporter: Where do you get bundles of new notes from...? Ruby: We buy them in black market... Reporter: Where do you get bundles of new notes from...? Ruby: They are sold at Ghanta Ghar... we buy from there... Reporter: If we go there to buy, how much would it cost...? Ruby: You go there and find out... how much it costs... Reporter: Still, how much will it cost...? Ruby: The rates there change daily... rates change immediately... Reporter: Oh... there's no fixed rate there...? Ruby: No... there's no fixed rate... From here, we learned that bundles of fresh notes are being sold in black in Kanpur's Ghantaghar area. The rates keep changing here daily. Now let's go to the fresh notes market and understand the black marketing... After this, we reached Ghantaghar. There were shops along the road. Most shops had no names. The shops only had written, torn, old notes exchanged here. We reached Anil Brothers. Here we met the shopkeeper Vijay. Vijay said that bank employees come and sell us bundles of fresh notes, we add our percentage and sell them to you. Reporter: Uncle... we are wedding planners... need bundles of new notes... Vijay: Yes, you people must need it... You'll get it... Reporter: How much will one bundle of 10 rupee notes (100 notes) cost...? Vijay: The 10 rupee one... will cost you 1370 rupees... Reporter: How much will the 20 rupee one cost...? Vijay: The 20 rupee one is more expensive... will cost 2480 rupees (100 notes of 20 rupees). Reporter: Will I get a bundle of 1 rupee notes...? Vijay: Yes... You'll get everything here... Reporter: How much will a bundle of old 1 rupee notes (100 notes) cost...? Vijay: 1 rupee bundle... you'll get it for 1400 rupees (100 notes of 1 rupee)... and 5 rupee bundle will cost 1300 rupees (100 notes of 5 rupees)... Reporter: Will I also get bundles of 100 rupees and 50 rupees...? Vijay: 100 rupee bundle... you'll get it by paying 120 rupees extra... 50 rupee bundle will cost 5170 rupees (100 notes of 50 rupees)... From Vijay's words, it became clear that this market has all kinds of fresh notes. Just need to pay an extra price for all of them. Now we wanted to know how many fresh notes are here? How do they come here? When we talked to Vijay for the answer, he told us that you can get as many as you want. Bank employees themselves come and give them. 10 lakhs... 5 lakhs... you can get as many fresh notes as you want Vijay: Rates go up and down daily... less-more... Reporter: But we need it in bulk... meaning we need more... Vijay: How much more do you need... need 10 lakhs... need 5 lakhs... you'll get it now... just count the payment... Reporter: Actually... we went to the bank... submitted applications too... but they said... it's not available now... Vijay: You won't get bundles in the bank... You can get bundles of 100 rupees in the bank... Reporter: We went to the bank and got very troubled... but didn't get it... they said - will give when it comes... Vijay: They'll give when it comes... here commission will be charged... everything will be available... those b@$#@#$ give everything here... all bank officials give it here... no outsider gives it... when we are buying from bank people here by paying them more money, why would they give it to you...? The shopkeeper Vijay's words exposed their collusion with bank officials. Now we wanted to know how much bank officials earn in this black mailing? When we continued the conversation with Vijay, he said - Bank officials also earn good money. He also said that online transactions don't work here, all transactions are done in cash. Bank officials charge 3500 rupees extra for 1000 fresh notes Reporter: How much will bank officials get for 1 bundle (100 new notes)...? Vijay: If bank officials give you a bundle of fresh notes (10 bundles), they won't get anything... here they get Rs 350 for 1 bundle of 100 notes, meaning they get Rs 3500 extra for 1 bundle (10 bundles = 1000 new notes)... so why would they give it to you...? Reporter: Is this why they don't give it to us...? Vijay: Bank officials don't give it to customers... they all bring it here... Reporter: Well... Do you need to be informed in advance, or will it be available immediately...? Vijay: Will get it immediately... Tell me now... What all do you need... Will give right now... What will we do with so many notes... Reporter: We take wedding contracts... Client demands.... Vijay: Then what's the problem... Take 50 thousand extra from them... Everything will be arranged... Reporter: Okay... Will you accept online payment...? Vijay: Cash payment works here... Online doesn't work here... Reporter: It's used in garlands too, right...? Vijay: Garland... Jaymala... Notes are used in everything... Show the money... You'll get all the goods... Whatever you want... You'll get it... Vijay's words made it clear that there is no shortage of fresh notes in the market. Now we wanted to know which is the most expensive fresh note? In response, Vijay showed us a 1-rupee note. Said- these 100 notes will cost 2700 rupees. Old bundle of 1 rupee costs 1500 rupees, new bundle will cost 2700 rupees Reporter: For 1 rupee... will you get a bundle of old notes... or new notes...? Vijay: Both are available... old note bundle costs 1500 rupees... new note bundle costs 2700 rupees... Reporter: Hey... 2700 rupees... it will only have 100 notes in it, right...? Vijay: Yes... It will only have 100 notes... Reporter: Okay... now new ones won't be coming, right...? Vijay: The bank has no stock... clerks and officers keep everything at their homes... Reporter: Oh... bank clerks keep it at home...? Vijay: All officers keep it at their homes... when they're getting the money, why would they give it to anyone else...? Vijay claims that bank officers keep fresh notes at their homes instead of in banks. They are bringing these to the market and selling them. Now let's go to the bank, are fresh notes available here or not? After leaving the fresh notes market, we reached the bank. We wanted to know if fresh notes were available here or not. We reached HDFC Bank in Kalyanpur, Kanpur. Here we told the bank employee that there's a wedding at home and we need fresh notes. To this, the cashier said - Fresh notes are not available immediately. Come after January 14th with the wedding card and application. If bundles are available, we will give them. You won't get too many. We will try to give you one bundle. Meanwhile, when the Bhaskar team went to the State Bank of India Swaroop Nagar branch and demanded bundles of crisp notes, the bank employee said, go to your home branch and talk about it there. If bundles are available at the branch, you will get them. Banks are giving fresh notes, will take action if bank employees are selling notes in market Kanpur Lead Bank Manager Aditya Chandra said - So far, no such complaint has been received where bank employees were found selling fresh notes in the market. If such a case comes up, action will be taken against the bank employee. If customers demand fresh notes while withdrawing large amounts for weddings, bundles of new notes are provided. It depends on the rapport between the customer and the bank on how many fresh notes they receive.

summary: CGST Inspector Named in Rs 100 Crore GST Evasion Case: उत्तर प्रदेश में सामने आए करीब 100 करोड़ रुपये के जीएसटी चोरी मामले ने कर विभाग और प्रशासनिक हलकों में हड़कंप मचा दिया है। इस हाई-प्रोफाइल मामले में दिल्ली में तैनात केंद्रीय जीएसटी (CGST) इंस्पेक्टर को आरोपी बनाया गया है। उत्तर प्रदेश स्पेशल टास्क फोर्स (STF) द्वारा जुटाए गए नए और पुख्ता साक्ष्यों के आधार पर इंस्पेक्टर मोहित अग्रवाल का नाम गाजियाबाद के कवि नगर थाने में दर्ज एफआईआर में शामिल किया गया है। एसटीएफ के अनुसार, आरोपी इंस्पेक्टर फिलहाल फरार है और उसकी गिरफ्तारी के लिए कई टीमें लगाई गई हैं। मामले में अब तक चार आरोपियों को गिरफ्तार किया जा चुका है, जबकि जांच का दायरा लगातार बढ़ता जा रहा है।

title: UP CM Yogi gets lion-themed chair:Saffron seat made from Kedarnath, featuring carvings inspired by Uttarakhand temples
summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will now sit on a special lion-themed chair. The chair is unique as it has been crafted from leftover deodar wood from the Kedarnath reconstruction project. It reflects intricate carvings inspired by temples in Uttarakhand and also emits a natural fragrance, meaning it spreads a pleasant aroma wherever it is placed. The chair has been gifted by Uttarakhand Minister of State (Colonel Retd) Ajay Kothiyal. He handed it over to Yogi Adityanath in Gorakhpur on January 15, on the occasion of Makar Sankranti. Presented to him in his capacity as Mahant, the chair was well received and has been installed in the main auditorium of the Gorakhnath Temple. Special chair made from leftover deodar wood from Kedarnath Colonel Ajay Kothiyal said that deodar wood was used on a large scale during the Kedarnath reconstruction project. Some of that wood was left over. He said that he got the idea to use this wood to make something related to a sacred and religious place. In this sequence, he decided to get a special deodar chair made for Yogi Adityanath. Temple-inspired cedar chair design The chair was designed by architect Krishna Kudiyal, who studied the architecture of Uttarakhand’s temples before finalising the design. It was crafted by a traditional wood artisan from Kota village near Chakrata after about 15 days of meticulous work. The chair features lion figures embossed on both armrests as symbols of power, while the back showcases carvings inspired by Uttarakhand’s temple architecture. Use of saffron colour, inclusion of Mahasu Temple's woodwork Colonel Kothiyal stated that an attempt has been made to primarily incorporate the woodwork art of Mahasu Temple into the chair. Additionally, Yogi Adityanath's favorite saffron color has also been used in the chair's form. He informed that this chair was presented to Yogi Adityanath as a Mahant, and he liked it very much. This is why it has been installed in the main auditorium of Gorakhnath Temple. Yogi's ancestral village in Pauri Another special feature of this particular chair is that due to the deodar wood, its sweet scent also spreads throughout the hall. Yogi Adityanath also has an old connection with Uttarakhand. He is originally a resident of Panchur village in Yamkeshwar block of Pauri district. Who is Colonel Ajay Kothiyal? Colonel Ajay Kothiyal has been the face of the Kedarnath Reconstruction Project. He played a crucial role in the reconstruction of the Dham after the 2013 Kedarnath disaster. After this, he contested the 2022 assembly elections as the chief ministerial candidate from the Aam Aadmi Party, but was unsuccessful. After that, he joined the BJP. Currently, he holds the status of a Minister of State in the Uttarakhand government.

title: Forcibly retired IPS receives death threat in Deoria jail:Letter found hidden under stone; ex-officer on hunger strike
summary: UP's forcibly retired IPS officer Amitabh Thakur received a death threat in Deoria jail on Friday. He found a letter, typed on a computer, hidden under a stone outside his barrack. He immediately informed the jail administration about this. The jail superintendent informed the DM-SP and initiated an investigation. However, jail officials are reluctant to comment. Amitabh Thakur has been imprisoned since December 10 in a fraud case. He has been on a hunger strike in jail for the past two days. Read the lawyer's letter Know in detail Advocate Praveen Dwivedi said that former IPS officer Amitabh Thakur has been lodged in jail since December 10 in a land allocation case related to the Industrial Area and has been on a hunger strike for the past two days. He is demanding CCTV footage and CDRs from the time of his arrest, which, according to him, have not been provided. Dwivedi stated that during his meeting, Amitabh Thakur appeared extremely frightened and revealed that he had found a computer-typed letter containing a clear death threat hidden under a stone outside his barrack. Following this, he has been feeling mentally distressed and insecure. Thakur immediately informed the jail authorities and handed over the threatening letter and the stone. The lawyer termed the incident very serious, especially in a high-security jail, and expressed concern that his client’s life could be in real danger. Court appearance on January 17 The decision on Amitabh Thakur's bail application is still pending. Advocate Praveen Dwivedi had demanded Amitabh Thakur's appearance during the hearing of the bail application in the District Judge's court on January 17. The court accepted this and ordered the accused to be produced. Sudden illness on January 6 Case in which the former IPS was arrested Former IPS officer Amitabh Thakur was arrested late on the night of December 9 from Shahjahanpur railway station. This arrest is related to a 26-year-old plot allocation in Deoria. Forcibly retired 7 years before retirement Outside Amitabh Thakur’s residence, a board reads 'Forcibly Retired IPS.' In fact, his retirement was due in 2028, but during his service, he faced several departmental inquiries. On the state government’s recommendation, the Union Home Ministry ordered his compulsory retirement. The central government had screened his service record and concluded that he was not fit to continue in government service. After this decision, Thakur put up the board outside his house. He later became active in politics and continued to frequently clash with the government on various issues.

title: UP Evening Wrap:BJP nears victory in Mumbai civic body polls; UP leaders play key role in Maharashtra civic polls more
summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. BJP nears victory in Mumbai civic body polls, Thackeray family's 30-year rule to end For the first time in Mumbai's history, the BJP may have a mayor. In the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) election results, the BJP alliance has a lead in 118 of the 227 seats. Of these, the BJP is leading in 90 seats, and the Shiv Sena-led Shinde is leading in 28. 2. Brawl over 'Prabhat Pheri' in Badaun: police-villager clash leaves women injured, procession allowed under supervision A clash erupted between police and villagers in Byor Kasimabad, Badaun, on Friday over a 'Prabhat Pheri' route dispute. Police stopped the procession, leading to pushing and shoving, and dispersed the crowd with batons. The procession was later allowed under supervision. 3. Where Shah Jahan and Mumtaz are actually buried: true graves 22 feet below Taj Mahal dome, entry restricted The Taj Mahal, famed for its marble, colored inlay work, and architecture, conceals the true graves of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz 22 feet below the main dome. Entry to this burial chamber is not allowed, though the structure continues to narrate their story. 4. Venezuelan leader, Machado, presents her Nobel Peace Prize to Trump Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado said on Thursday that she presented her Nobel Peace Prize medal to US President Donald Trump during a meeting at the White House. 5. UP leaders play key role in Maharashtra civic polls: 30 lakh migrant voters influence results UP leaders, especially from eastern UP, campaigned actively in Maharashtra civic elections to attract about 30 lakh UP-origin voters. The Samajwadi Party fielded candidates in high-density migrant areas, with prominent leaders staying in Mumbai for several days. 6. UP minister tries to touch commissioner’s feet during Lalitpur overbridge visit, stopped by officer Minister of State Manohar Lal Panth attempted to touch the feet of Jhansi Division Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey while inspecting an under-construction overbridge in Lalitpur on Thursday. The Commissioner stopped him and folded his hands, amusing the MLA and district officials. 7. Govt cracks down on illegal walkie-talkie sales citing threat to national security, ₹44 lakh fine on eight e-commerce companies The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties totaling ₹44 lakh on eight e-commerce companies, including Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, and Meta, for selling illegal walkie-talkies. The authority termed these sales a serious threat to national security. 8. Baba from masaura owns ₹50-crore ashram: brother murdered, story of Santosh Tiwari becoming Jagadguru Santosh Tiwari, from Masaura village in Lalitpur, Bundelkhand, lives in luxury with a ₹50-crore ashram, Land Rover Defender, Porsche Turbo, and Ray-Ban sunglasses. Often praised by UP CM Yogi, he rose to prominence despite his brother being murdered. 9. UP government promotes sports with basketball event: CM Yogi highlights jobs, rewards, and olympic culture In Gorakhpur, CM Yogi played basketball and inaugurated the inter-university women’s basketball tournament. He interacted with players, released gas balloons, and emphasised sports-related jobs, rewards, and fostering an Olympic culture in UP universities. 10. Kartik Aaryan returns ₹15 crore after failure of recent film ‘Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri’ at Box Office Kartik Aaryan and Ananya Panday's film 'Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri' was released in cinemas on December 25, 2025. However, the film did not perform as expected at the box office and proved to be a flop. Meanwhile, a report by Bollywood Hungama claims that after the film's failure, Kartik returned approximately ₹15 crore from his fees to the producers.

title: Massive fire in Lucknow, man jumps from apartment:Hangs from balcony for 10 minutes, people flee as smoke chokes building
summary: A massive fire broke out on Friday in Block 39 of the Basant Kunj Scheme in Thakurganj, Lucknow. The blaze spread rapidly and engulfed three floors of the building, filling the premises with thick smoke. Several people were trapped inside as panic gripped the area. In a desperate attempt to escape, some residents jumped from the building to save their lives. Eyewitnesses reported scenes of chaos, with people shouting for help as the fire raged. Four fire tenders were rushed to the spot and firefighting operations are underway to bring the blaze under control. Chief Fire Officer Anshu Mittal said a young man who was trapped inside the building was safely rescued by the fire brigade. The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained. Fire breaks out in Thakurganj area A massive fire broke out in a house in the Thakurganj area at around 2:30 pm on Friday. Within minutes, the flames engulfed the entire house. Seeing thick smoke and rising flames, local residents alerted the fire station. Fire tenders rushed to the spot and safely evacuated the people living in the house. The fire was brought under control by three fire brigade vehicles. Eyewitnesses said the fire started due to a sudden short circuit near an air conditioner. Smoke appeared first, followed by intense flames. The fire quickly spread to another part of the house. The fire brigade team, which reached the spot promptly, rescued the family members. Reports also suggest that the fire spread to three neighbouring houses.
