title: Uttar Pradesh Police revises transfer policy:Home district and range postings barred; compassionate transfers restricted to spouse cases
summary: The Uttar Pradesh Police has made a major change to its transfer policy for Sub-Inspectors and Constables recruited up to the 2019 batch. Under the revised rules, transfers in general cases will now be considered only on compassionate grounds. Such transfers will be permitted exclusively in cases where both husband and wife are serving in the police force. The policy also makes it clear that no Inspector or Sub-Inspector will be posted in their home range, home district, or adjoining border district. For availing a compassionate transfer, both spouses must submit their police identity cards as proof. Officials said exemptions from the posting restrictions will be given only when both the husband and wife are working in the police department. The department has clarified that the changes aim to bring uniformity and transparency to postings. Transfers allowed for personnel recruited before 2019 The DGP said that for personnel recruited after the 2019 batch, transfers will be considered only in cases where both husband and wife are serving in the police department. As per the transfer policy dated June 22, 2018, no inspector or sub-inspector can be posted in their home range, home district or a district bordering their home district. Similarly, head constables and constables cannot be posted in their home district or a district adjoining their home district. Transfer policy was also changed before the Lok Sabha elections Ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the UP DGP had amended the transfer policy. Under this, police personnel who had completed three years in a district, or were due to complete three years by May 31, 2024, were transferred. Yogi government’s stand on posting husband and wife together Police couples posted in different districts face several difficulties, including family and practical issues. Keeping these problems in mind, and in line with the government’s transfer policy, efforts have been made to post husband and wife in the same district. On May 22, 2025, in the first phase, 101 constables were transferred under this policy. Female police personnel were posted in the districts where their husbands were posted, while male personnel were sent to the districts where their wives were serving. Earlier too, husband and wife had been posted in the same district on compassionate grounds, but the number of such cases was limited. This was the first time that such a large number of police personnel were transferred under this policy.

title: Leopard escapes during rescue, injures 4 in Kushinagar:Net tears as animal growls, forest staff loosen grip; search on with drones
summary: Four people, including a forest guard, were injured in a leopard attack in Kushinagar on Thursday. The leopard was trapped in wire fencing laid in a sugarcane field. When a forest department team reached the spot to rescue the animal, they laid a net, but it tore during the operation. As the leopard growled, forest workers loosened their grip, allowing it to escape. After breaking free, the leopard first attacked a forest guard and then a forest worker. A local youth intervened and saved the forest worker by hitting the animal with a stick. The leopard later attacked another villager and an employee of Wildlife Trust of India. Around 50 forest workers, including DFO Arun Kumar, are currently searching for the leopard. Six nets have been laid in nearby fields, and drones are being used for surveillance. The administration has appealed to people to stay away from the area and avoid provoking the animal. The incident took place in Siswa Gopal village under the Khadda police station area. First see 3 pictures- How the incident unfolded Village head Suresh’s brother, Indresh, said he was on his way to cut sugarcane when he spotted the leopard in Rajesh Lal Srivastava’s field. “The leopard tried to pounce, but it was trapped in the wire and could not attack. I raised an alarm. On hearing the noise, the leopard started growling,” he said. He added that villagers ran back and informed others. Soon, hundreds of people from nearby villages reached the spot. A team of five to seven forest personnel from Maharajganj district arrived and threw a net over the leopard. They then began cutting the wire with a sickle. “When the leopard growled, the forest workers got scared and loosened their grip,” Indresh said. Leopard attacks forest staff and villagers The leopard escaped through a torn portion of the net and first attacked the forest guard, injuring his foot. He was saved when people nearby beat the animal with sticks. The leopard then pounced on a forest worker. Villager Krishnandan Kumar intervened and struck the leopard with a stick, saving the worker’s life. The animal also attacked Angad, a local youth, and Arshad Hussain, project head of Wildlife Trust of India in Maharajganj. All injured were taken for treatment. Villagers allege negligence by forest department After the incident, villagers accused the forest department of negligence. Nizamuddin, a local resident, said the leopard escaped because the team used a torn net. “The forest department came with a damaged net. The leopard escaped through the same torn section while attacking people,” he alleged. Angad, who was injured, said the situation worsened due to crowd noise. “People were shouting, and some children climbed trees to make videos. The leopard became uncontrollable and attacked me while escaping,” he said. Another villager said sugarcane peeling and cutting work was underway in nearby fields. “If the leopard had not been trapped, a major accident could not have been ruled out,” he said. Forest department says noise led to failure Forest officials said the rescue attempt failed due to heavy crowding. Nichaul Range forest worker Mahatma said villagers gathered at the rescue site despite appeals to stay away. “Because of the noise, the leopard attacked forest workers and fled. The team tried its best to capture it,” he said. DFO Arun Singh said a team from Gorakhpur Zoo has been called, and forest staff from Maharajganj are assisting in the operation. “The leopard is still in the area. Search operations are underway, and it will be caught soon,” he said.

title: Scorpio runs over six at 100 kmph in Chandauli:5 vehicles crushed in 10 seconds, angry crowd assaults driver
summary: A speeding Scorpio car went out of control in Chandauli and hit five vehicles within seconds, before running over six pedestrians. The impact was severe, leaving vehicles badly damaged and debris scattered across the road. Some people were thrown several feet away, causing panic at the spot. After the collisions, the Scorpio rammed into a divider. Locals pulled the driver out of the vehicle and thrashed him. Three other people were inside the car. All four were reportedly drunk. The crowd later handed them over to the police. Police reached the scene and shifted the injured to a trauma centre and Ramnagar Hospital. One young man died during treatment. The condition of the other injured remains critical. The incident took place near Padav intersection in the Mughalsarai police station area, about 23 kilometres from the district headquarters in Chandauli. 4 pictures of the accident... Now read step by step how the Scorpio created havoc on the road One dead, others in critical condition Six people injured in the collision were taken by ambulance to Lal Bahadur Shastri District Hospital. Doctors there declared cyclist Irshad Ahmad (25) dead. Four seriously injured persons were referred to the trauma centre for advanced treatment. The injured include Mohammad Islam (20), a resident of Kutban Shahid Peelikothi under Kotwali police station, Varanasi, and Salman (36), a resident of Sujabad under Ramnagar police station. After initial treatment, both were referred to Kabirchowra Divisional Hospital. Two other injured persons are yet to be identified. Police said Irshad, son of Jaleel, was a resident of Chaurhat village. He was returning home on his bicycle after buying medicine from a medical store. Irshad was unemployed and helped his father in farming. Search for car owner underway Arun Kumar Singh said the car owner has been identified through the registration number WB 02 8586. The Scorpio is registered in the name of Rakesh Yadav. The accused driver, Harish Yadav, a resident of Badi Piyari under Chowk police station in Varanasi, has been taken into custody. Police said the occupants of the vehicle were allegedly intoxicated at the time of the incident. The damaged Scorpio was removed from the spot using a crane and taken to the police post. Further investigation in the case is underway.

title: Out-of-syllabus questions asked in ANM recruitment examination:Over 1,000 candidates protest in Lucknow, march towards CM’s residence
summary: Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) ANM (5272 posts) recruitment exam sparked anger among candidates in Lucknow. More than 1000 candidates protested outside the Pickup Building, alleging that questions were asked from outside the declared syllabus. They submitted a memorandum addressed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to the officials. Some candidates reached near the CM's residence. Gautampalli police is trying to reason with them and gathering information about their demands. 'Questions from outside the syllabus appeared in the exam held on January 11' Candidates say that the Health Worker (Female) ANM recruitment examination was conducted on January 11, 2026. Questions were asked from outside the official and declared syllabus issued by the commission. About 35 to 40 questions were included from General Knowledge (GK) and Computer subjects, while these subjects were not mentioned in the syllabus. 'Months of preparation wasted' The protesting candidates said that they had worked hard for many months according to the syllabus set by the commission. Not only did their hard work go to waste due to out-of-syllabus questions in the exam, but questions have also been raised about the fairness, transparency, and credibility of the entire recruitment process. High-level investigation demanded from Chief Minister The candidates submitted a memorandum addressed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to the officers. In it, they demanded that a high-level investigation be conducted into the GK and computer questions asked outside the syllabus in the UPSSSC ANM (5272) recruitment exam. Keeping in mind the future of candidates, the exam should be cancelled, and re-exam dates should be announced soon. Large crowd gathered outside pickup building During the demonstration, a large number of candidates gathered outside the pickup building, causing temporary disorder in the area. The candidates say that if their demands are not acted upon soon, they will intensify their protest. So far, no official response has come from the commission or administration on the matter, but amid growing pressure, all eyes are now fixed on the government's next move. Now read what the candidates said... Kanchan Yadav, a candidate who participated in the protest, said that the commission had given 38 topics. It was said that questions would come only from those topics. 40 questions in the exam came from outside the syllabus. We have only one demand - that the exam should be conducted again. Khushboo Pathak, a candidate from Varanasi, said that only 50 to 60 questions in the exam were from the syllabus. The remaining questions were out of the syllabus. The questions were of UPSC level. Our demand from the government is that the exam should be conducted again.

title: UP Bar Council Elections begin in Agra:Voting will continue for 2 days, 4,900 advocates will exercise their vote
summary: The excitement for Uttar Pradesh Bar Council elections is at its peak today. Voting for the state's largest lawyers' organization has begun today in four phases. Under the first phase, voting is underway in the Agra district on Thursday. Lawyers will exercise their voting rights to select 25 members. A total of 333 candidates are in the fray from across the state in the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council elections. Meanwhile, 11 candidates are contesting from the Agra district. The first phase of voting in Agra will be completed today and tomorrow, that is, January 16 and 17. Across the state, a total of 2,49,808 COP (Certificate of Practice) holding advocates are eligible to vote, while in the Agra district, a total of 4,900 advocates will exercise their voting rights. Voting arrangements have been made for two days at the District Court (Civil Complex) and Fatehabad Court (Bagh Badshahi) in Agra. ADJ-26 Amarjeet has been appointed as the election officer for voting at the District Court, and Civil Judge Kishan Chand Pandey has been appointed at the Fatehabad Court. At the Civil Complex, advocates practicing in Collectorate, Commissionery, Taxation, Tehsil Sadar, Kirawali, and Etmadpur are casting their votes. Uttar Pradesh Bar Council elections are being conducted in four phases. The first phase is today, January 16-17, the second phase January 20-21, the third phase January 27-28, and the final phase will be completed in Prayagraj on January 30-31. From the Agra district, Durg Vijay Singh Bhaiya, Arvind Mishra, Harjeet Arora, Saroj Yadav, Radha Yadav, Neha Gupta, Anup Sharma, Mukesh Sharma, Puran Singh Rajput, R.S. Maurya, and Tej Singh Baghel are candidates. All candidates have been visiting lawyers across 80 districts of the state for a long time, appealing for first preference votes. The nomination fee for the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council election is higher than that of the MP, MLA, and Presidential elections. Each candidate has deposited Rs 1.50 lakh as a nomination fee and Rs 25 thousand for voter lists of 80 districts with the Bar Council. During campaigning, new law books, diaries, calendars, etc., are also being distributed to lawyers. The civil court premises appear covered with banners and posters. This election is being monitored by a High Power Committee constituted by the Supreme Court. The committee is chaired by former Chief Justice of Jharkhand Justice Ravi Ranjan. Former judge of Allahabad High Court S.R. Masuri and former judge of Delhi High Court Rekha Palli are included as members. The state's election officer is former judge of Allahabad High Court Arvind Kumar Tripathi, while former judge Surendra Singh is appointed as observer. Former Chairman P.K. Singh's Appeal Former Chairman of Uttar Pradesh Bar Council, P.K. Singh, made an emotional appeal to Agra lawyers, saying that the lawyers of Agra honored him by making him a member five times and chairman once. He said that lawyers should give priority to local candidates because local members are the ones who help in times of need. P.K. Singh said that this time, 11 candidates are in the fray from Agra. Lawyers should first vote for candidates from their district in order of priority, then support outside candidates. He expressed confidence that if voting is done wisely, the number of members elected from Agra could increase.

title: Protests erupt over Manikarnika Ghat dispute:Congress says, 'Kashi's heritage is being destroyed'; experts say good that PMO took cognizance
summary: The alleged historical breaking of the jewel at Manikarnika Ghat in Kashi has now taken a political turn. The accusations of damaging religious sites and heritage associated with Maa Ahilyabai Holkar have further intensified the matter. Protests are happening from Kashi to Indore. On Friday, the Congress party also came forward openly. Congress officials reached the District Magistrate's office and submitted a memorandum demanding an impartial investigation of the entire matter. Party leaders say that cultural and historical heritage is being damaged in Varanasi in the name of development. BJP people destroyed age-old heritage- Ajay Rai On Friday, UP Congress president Ajay Rai spoke to the media in Delhi and levelled serious allegations over demolition being carried out in the name of Kashi heritage. He alleged that the Modi–Yogi government is engaged in completely destroying Kashi’s ancient heritage and one of the greatest legacies of Hinduism. Ajay Rai said Kashi represents the biggest heritage of Hindu religion, but the central and state governments have ruined it. He claimed that in the name of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, Baba Vishwanath’s courtyard has been turned into something resembling a modern mall and hundreds of ancient temples have been demolished. Referring specifically to the Akshay Vat tree, Ajay Rai said Hindu tradition considers Kashi, Gaya (Bodh Gaya) and Prayagraj as a single sacred trio. He said these places were home to thousands-of-years-old Akshay Vat trees, and Indian history speaks of three such sacred Akshay Vats. He added that even Prime Minister Narendra Modi pays obeisance to the Akshay Vat trees, and only two now remain at Gaya and the Prayagraj Sangam. The Akshay Vat in Kashi, he alleged, was completely sliced and cut down. Rai claimed the tree existed even before Baba Vishwanath and Maa Parvati came to Kashi, but it was destroyed by contractors from Gujarat. Religious places not being spared in Varanasi - Congress Congress Metropolitan President Raghavendra Chaubey said - In Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency Varanasi, first hundreds of temples were demolished in the name of Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, then the Sarvaseva Sangh Ashram connected to the freedom struggle heritage was destroyed. Now in the Dalmandi area, where the livelihood of about ten thousand people is connected, demolition is being carried out. After this, allegations have now emerged about damaging religious sites, idols, and artworks built by Maa Ahilyabai Holkar at Manikarnika Ghat. Good that PMO took coznigence- Prof. A K Joshi Meanwhile, senior retired sociology professor at BHU, Dr A J Joshi, said the steps taken by the administration are part of the ghat’s mega makeover plan, but the exercise reflects a failure to learn from past mistakes and a lack of adequate groundwork before the demolition began. Notably, Dr Joshi has earlier been part of the Manikarnika Tirth Vikas Samiti that undertook the works and planning related ghat improvement. Speaking to Bhaskar English, he said the controversy forced the PMO and the local administration to come out with explanations after protests erupted. Dr Joshi added that it was reassuring the issue was addressed in time and that instructions have now been issued to reinstall the historic statues once the makeover is completed. Truth should be brought out through investigation Congress has demanded that the administration disclose the truth of the entire matter before the public. For this, a joint delegation has demanded a site inspection, which should include the district administration, local citizens, and Congress representatives. The party has warned that if action is not taken within a week, Congress members will be forced to start a relay hunger strike and then an indefinite hunger strike. State spokesperson Sanjeev Singh said - The administration should investigate the entire matter with transparency. If our heritage is not secured, Congress will not sit quietly, and the movement will be intensified. Rajeshwar Singh Patel, Raghavendra Choubey, Fasahat Hussain Babu, Sanjeev Singh, Dr. Rajesh Gupta, Satnam Singh, Ashok Singh, Dilip Choubey, Santosh Chaurasia, Hasan Mehdi Kabban, Piyush Srivastava, Khalid Siddiqui, Ramkesh Yadav, Santosh Maurya, Lokesh Singh, Manoj Verma, Manu, Rohit Dubey, and Arvind Kumar attended the program. All recovered artifacts have been preserved Meanwhile, the administration has given clarification regarding these allegations. The administration says that the first phase of construction work is ongoing, and during this time, whatever artifacts have been obtained have been safely kept in the Gurudham temple. The Culture Department is examining it, and in the future, it will be reinstalled with full reverence and respect. PMO and CMO have also taken cognizance of the matter Under the redevelopment project of Manikarnika Ghat crematorium, after a video surfaced showing the destruction of an ancient platform by a bulldozer on Tuesday, revealing the statue of Rajmata Ahilyabai Holkar and floral-leaf designs and other artworks on the steps in the debris, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) and Chief Minister's Office have taken notice of the resulting controversy. title: Brawl over 'Prabhat Pheri' in Badaun:Police–villager clash over route dispute; women injured, procession later allowed under supervision
summary: A clash broke out between police and villagers in Badaun on Friday over a 'Prabhat-Pheri', leading to a tense situation and allegations of a lathi charge. The incident occurred in Byor Kasimabad, under the Islamnagar police station area. Police stopped the procession, citing a dispute over the route. This led to pushing and shoving, after which police dispersed the crowd using batons. Villagers alleged that police carried out a lathi charge in which women and youths were also injured. The situation remained tense for about an hour. On receiving information, SP Rural Dr Hridayesh Katheria and SDM Bisauli Rashi Krishna reached the spot and brought the situation under control. Later, the morning procession was taken out under police and administrative supervision. Villagers claimed they have been using the same route for the procession for the past 50 years. Know the full matter A morning procession of the Magh month was taken out in Byor Kasimabad village under the Islamnagar police station area on Friday morning. Villagers said the procession has been following the same route for nearly 50 years. However, after complaints from people of another community, police from Islamnagar reached the village around 5 am. Police attempted to stop the procession, declaring the route disputed. This led to a clash between villagers and the police. As tensions rose, police teams from Bilsi and Ughaiti were called to the spot, and a PAC unit was also deployed. The situation soon went out of control. SDM Bisauli Rashi Krishna and CO Bilsi arrived at the scene to manage the situation. Around 8 am, police resorted to a lathi charge, triggering panic in the village. Several women and young men were injured and were admitted to the community health centre for treatment. A day earlier, members of the other community had also objected to the procession and lodged complaints with the police. SP Rural convinced villagers and got the procession taken out Following the incident, heavy police deployment was made in the village to maintain law and order. After receiving information, SP Rural Dr Hridayesh Katheria reached the spot and tried to pacify the villagers. However, residents protested and demanded action against the police personnel and officials who had stopped the procession. After prolonged arguments, the police stepped back and allowed the morning procession to proceed under police and administrative supervision. Even after the procession concluded, families of the injured women and youths continued to press for action against those responsible. SP Rural Dr Hridayesh Katheria said the procession was initially stopped due to opposition from some people. Later, it was found that the procession had been using the same route for many years. After this, the procession was allowed to proceed safely. He added that there would be no restriction on the morning procession in the future and villagers had been informed accordingly. Villagers took out procession through old route According to villagers, the Prabhat Pheri has been taken out in the village for several decades. They said that about ten years ago, during the SP government, the route was changed following objections from a particular community. This time, when villagers resumed the procession on the old route, members of that community objected again and informed the police, leading to the confrontation.

title: UP government boosts sports with basketball event launch:CM Yogi highlights sports jobs, rewards, and pushes for Olympics culture across UP universities
summary: Yogi played basketball in Gorakhpur. Like players, he bounced the ball twice on the basketball court, then tossed it into the basket. Along with this, the CM inaugurated the inter-university women's basketball tournament. The CM also got acquainted with the players and released gas balloons in the sky. The CM said- Before 2014, sports competitions were not on the government's agenda. Players either migrated or sat frustrated and discouraged. Today we are conducting sports competitions in every village. All the means of life can only be obtained through a healthy body. A healthy body will only exist when it remains in discipline and restraint. The women's basketball tournament at Deendayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University will be held from January 15 to 19. A total of 31 university teams from 14 states of the eastern region are participating in it. Read CM Yogi's 4 major points- 1- We have given jobs to more than 500 athletes CM Yogi said - We are building sports grounds in every gram panchayat in UP. Now, not only does the Government of India give awards to athletes who win medals in the Olympics, Commonwealth, and Asian Games, but state governments also give awards. So far, we have provided jobs to more than 500 athletes in different departments of the state. Deputy SP, Tehsildar, and Regional Sports Officer - 6 posts are being given directly to players. Sports activities should not just be a foundation, it should not remain just a formality, but should become part of daily routine. For this, more than 96 thousand sports kits have been given to youth clubs and women's clubs in the state. 2- All universities should prepare players Yogi said - I appeal to all universities to adopt at least one sport and prepare players for it. Develop healthy competition. If this happens, youth will stay away from drugs and all kinds of perversions. When youth play, they prosper. The state's first Sports University has been built in Meerut. The Chauri-Chaura incident in the freedom movement, which shook the foreign rule, was also connected to the land of Gorakhpur. This was the workplace of Munshi Premchand. 3- Government gives 6 crore rupees to gold medal winners Today, many families have made sports a part of their lives. Parents no longer discriminate between sons and daughters. When a player from UP qualifies for the Olympics, we provide them with Rs 10 lakh assistance and a sports kit. If they win a gold medal, the government gives Rs 6 crore for individual sports, along with a Class-1 job. For team games, the government gives Rs 3 crore for a gold medal. Silver medal winners receive Rs 3 crore for individual sports and Rs 1.5 crore for team games. Similar incentive amounts are given for bronze medals as well. 4- We wish for the 2036 Olympics to be held in India Whenever any Indian team goes anywhere, they receive all kinds of encouragement from the Prime Minister. When they return victorious, he personally meets everyone. We need to start preparing from today for the Commonwealth Games in India in 2030. Under PM Modi's leadership, we all wish for the 2036 Olympics to be held in India. We also hope that Indian athletes will win the maximum number of medals.

title: Jeweler commits suicide in Lucknow:Body found hanging in courtyard, victim depressed over rising Gold and Silver prices
summary: A jeweller in the Lucknow Chowk area committed suicide by hanging. He was depressed due to rising gold and silver prices. He was found hanging in the courtyard of his house. Police have sent the body for a post-mortem. Manoj Agarwal, a resident of Chauptiya, worked with silver. He had a shop in Kundan Market near Hari Masjid in Chowk Sarrafa Market. On Thursday, he was at the shop in the afternoon. He participated in the Makar Sankranti feast happening in Chowk. After that, he closed the shop and went home. At night, he was found hanging from a grill in the house's courtyard. Gold-silver should be freed from futures trading When family members saw him hanging, they started screaming. Hearing the screams, nearby people gathered. After this, the police were informed. Police arrived at the scene, took possession of the body, and sent it for post-mortem. Investigation reveals depression due to continuous fluctuation in gold-silver prices. Currently, police are investigating the matter. Chowk Sarafa Association General Secretary Vinod Maheshwari said that due to a price surge in the jewelry trade, he committed suicide by hanging due to depression. There is a demand from the Government of India to free silver-gold from futures trading. Artisan traders from Rajkot, Agra, Kanpur, and Lucknow are on the verge of ruin.

title: Young man commits suicide by shooting himself in Lucknow:Cheated millions in the name of government job, took money from roommate also
summary: A young man who cheated millions in the name of government jobs in Lucknow committed suicide by shooting himself. His blood-soaked body was found in a rented room. When his roommate arrived there, the door was locked from inside. When the police arrived at the information and broke down the door, his blood-soaked body was lying on the bed. When the shawl was removed, blood was flowing from his chest. A revolver was lying nearby. Police sent the body for a post-mortem. The incident took place around 8 PM on Thursday in Vikas Nagar Sector-L. Pradyuman Pathak was a resident of Jaunpur. In a preliminary police investigation, it has come to light that the young man had taken lakhs of rupees from many people in the name of getting government jobs. He had also taken money from his roommate in the name of getting a police job. Now people were asking for their money back. Shot in the chest, revolver found lying nearby Police said that in the evening, they received information on Dial 112 that a person had locked himself in a room in Sector L, Vikasnagar. Upon receiving the information, Vikasnagar police station immediately reached the spot. When the police team broke down the door and went inside, the young man was lying unconscious on the bed. Blood was coming out of his chest. An illegal revolver was lying nearby. He was immediately sent to the hospital for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. During police interrogation, it was revealed that Pradyuman previously lived in Mumbai. He had taken money from many people by claiming to influence government administration and promising government jobs. He had also taken about one and a half lakh rupees from his roommate, Divyanshu, for getting him a job in the police department. ACP said - CDR investigation will be done ACP Ghazipur Anidya Vikram Singh said that important evidence, including a revolver, mobile phone, has been seized from the crime scene. Call details will be obtained and investigated. The deceased was married and had a wife and a child. Further action will be taken after the arrival of family members. Roommate said - Called out, poured water from window Roommate Divyanshu said - I had been living with Pradyuman for 2 months. I had gone to Gomti Nagar's Patrakar Puram for some work. When I returned, the room was locked from inside. Knocked on the door for a long time. Called also, but got no response from inside. Then poured water towards Pradyuman's bed from the window, but there was no movement. After this, the police were informed. Pradyuman had taken money from many people in the name of providing government jobs. He would receive calls from creditors from morning to evening. People were asking for their money back when they didn't get jobs. He had been under stress for many days due to this matter.

title: Fog returns in UP, eight accidents, 24 vehicles collide:Schools shut in 5 districts; rain alert from tomorrow
summary: The weather has changed again in Uttar Pradesh, with intense cold and dense fog gripping large parts of the state. On Friday morning, thick fog covered at least 35 districts, including Lucknow and Barabanki. In many areas, visibility dropped to near zero, severely affecting road traffic. Schools of the 5 districts till 8th class will remain close till January 17. Due to poor visibility, 8 major accidents were reported across the state in a single day. As many as 24 vehicles collided at different locations. One person lost his life, while around 40 others were injured. Details of accidents reported from different districts: Why did the weather change? Find out Now, know the condition of cities- Lucknow: Fog appeared this morning after a week. The icy winds have increased the chill. There are chances of rain from tomorrow (January 17). On Thursday, the maximum temperature was 20.7°C and the minimum temperature was 5.5°C. This is 1.6 degrees below normal. Gorakhpur: Light fog and bitter cold were observed in Gorakhpur. The cold was so severe that people were seen taking refuge in bonfires and thick woolen clothes. Meteorologists have warned of dense fog for 2-3 more days. Due to fog, 22 trains are running late by 2 to 15 hours. Aligarh: Dense fog has enveloped Aligarh. Visibility dropped to just 10 meters. A cold wave moving at a speed of 8 km per hour increased the chill. The minimum temperature was recorded at 6 degrees and the maximum at 18 degrees. AQI was recorded at 207. Kanpur: Some areas experienced dense fog while others had light fog. People were seen shivering from the piercing cold. Cold winds increased people's difficulties further. Visibility remained low on Friday morning compared to the last six days. The minimum temperature was recorded at 9 °C. Weather experts say that the cold will continue to trouble for a few more days. Saharanpur: Dense fog prevailed in the morning. Visibility remained zero. The minimum temperature was recorded at 3°C and the maximum temperature at 12°C. AQI is 360. According to the meteorological department, fluctuations in the weather will be seen till January 20. Meerut: There was dense fog in the morning. Vehicle drivers faced difficulty on the road due to the visibility being 50 meters. The minimum temperature was recorded at 5.1 degrees. The sun is expected to come out during the day today. Agra: There was relief from fog, but icy winds increased the chill. Morning temperature remained at 6 °C. Many trains, including New Delhi-Khajuraho Vande Bharat and New Delhi-Bhopal Shatabdi, were delayed due to fog. AQI was recorded at 322 on Friday morning. According to the weather department, there may be fog on January 17 and light rain on January 18-19. Etawah: Fog knocked again after 7 days. Dense fog enveloped early in the morning, which severely reduced visibility. Due to fog, the city's historic Victoria Hall also became invisible. The minimum temperature in the morning dropped to 5 degrees Celsius, which affected rail and road traffic. Farrukhabad: The severe cold continues. The sun had been shining for a week, but now fog has been setting in for two days, which has increased the cold further. Fog remained since Friday morning, and visibility was around 30 meters. The minimum temperature was recorded at 7 degrees and the maximum temperature at 22 degrees. Farmers say that fog is beneficial for the wheat crop. Know how the weather will be for the next three days

title: Dhirendra Shastri makes tea in shop, :Completes Kamdagiri Parikrama in Chitrakoot; to begin 'Katha' in Banda for 5 days
summary: Bageshwar Dham’s Peethadheeshwar, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, will narrate the Hanumant Katha for five days starting today in Banda. The event, continuing until January 20, has been fully prepared, with the katha pandal set 300 meters from his 5-star hotel stay. Earlier, Shastri performed a parikrama of Lord Kamdagiri in Chitrakoot, visiting temples and meeting devotees, who offered flowers and sought blessings, while children presented him with their artwork. Visited Hanuman Temple, made tea himself, Kamdagiri Maha-aarti During the circumambulation, Dhirendra Krishna Shastri reached the Hanuman temple in Bahra. Here, after darshan and worship, he made and drank tea with his own hands. During this time, a crowd of devotees gathered, and people appeared excited to catch a glimpse of him. After this, he reached the Kamdagiri Maha-aarti site, where he performed the proper aarti of Lord Kamdagiri mountain. The priests who performed the aarti were given offerings. He also gave money as prasad to children standing nearby. Circumambulation completed in 1 hour 20 minutes Dhirendra Krishna Shastri completed the Kamadgiri circumambulation in about 1 hour and 20 minutes. After the circumambulation, he said that it was his good fortune to get the opportunity to circumambulate Kamadgiri. He mentioned that this is not the first time he has visited Chitrakoot, many times, and Bageshwar Dham has a special spiritual connection with Chitrakoot. Gave message of peace and love Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri said the Bageshwar family promotes peace, love, and harmony, appealing to all communities to aid India’s development. He will deliver his first discourse in Bundelkhand on Friday in Banda, discussing social issues and personal guidance. On marriage, he said he will wed soon, urging people to live simply and naturally. After completing the Kamdagiri parikrama, he rested at Arogyadham, while devotees’ enthusiasm remained high late into the night. No VIP facility in the pandal It should be noted that under the guidance of BJP leader and Bundelkhand Youth Foundation founder Praveen Singh, the katha will begin today at Mawai Bypass ground, about 4 km from the city. A waterproof and fire safety-proof pandal has been set up using German hangar technology across 125 bighas for the katha. The pandal has seating arrangements for 50,000 devotees at once. The special thing is that there is no VIP facility in the pandal. All people will sit on the same carpet on the ground. A divine darbar will be held on January 18. See the pillar-less pandal The pandal is water and fire proof Praveen Singh said - The specialty of the pandal is that there is no pillar in its center, allowing thousands of devotees to have a direct view of the Vyaspeetha without any obstruction. This structure is completely waterproof and fire-resistant. Made of aluminum and high-quality synthetic fabric, the pandal is capable of withstanding strong winds and rain. Due to the increased height and modern design of the pandal, ventilation will remain even during crowding. This will prevent devotees from feeling suffocated. The pandal has been divided into 4 rows ABCD. In A, the organizing committee and other VIP guests will sit on the ground to listen to the katha. B is reserved for women coming as special guests. The C row will have a media gathering. And in D, all devotees will sit. Stage decorated with 50 kg flowers A grand stage has been prepared for Pt. Dhirendra Shastri in the pandal. A large picture of Lord Hanuman is placed on the backdrop. A sofa has been placed in front for Dhirendra Shastri. The stage has been decorated with 50 kg of flowers. The katha will start at 1 PM and continue till 5 PM in the evening. Bhandara will run for 24 hours Another pandal has been set up next to this one, where arrangements for 24-hour bhandara (food service) have been made for all devotees. The bhandara includes puri-sabzi and sweets. Additionally, accommodation arrangements have been made for devotees coming from outside. Entry will be with coconut and Hanuman Chalisa Devotees coming to listen to Pt. Dhirendra Shastri's discourse must bring a coconut and the Shri Hanuman Chalisa book. Entry to the pandal will be allowed only with these items. The entry for the discourse will be free for all devotees. Divine Court will be held on 18th During Pt. Dhirendra Shastri's discourse, a Divine Court will also be set up on January 18th. Here, devotees' slips will be drawn. The Divine Court will be set up within the discourse pandal itself. More than three thousand personnel deployed for security For the 5-day katha, around 600 police personnel from Banda as well as Hamirpur, Mahoba, and Chitrakoot, 2500 volunteers, and 200 Akhand Hind Force jawans have been deployed. These include 120 SHOs, 247 sub-inspectors, and the rest are constables. Grand Kalash Yatra taken out before the katha A grand Kalash Yatra was taken out on January 15 before the Hanumant Katha by Bageshwar Dham's Peethadheeshwar Acharya Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. 50 thousand devotees participated in it, with women being in the majority. Chants of 'Jai Shri Ram' continued during the Kalash Yatra that proceeded with music and drums. The Kalash Yatra started from Ramlila Ground and concluded at Rifle Club Ground after passing through major city roads. The 1-kilometer-long journey was joined by MLA Prakash Dwivedi from Banda Sadar. Flowers were showered from drones during the yatra.

title: Mulayam Singh isolated as Mayawati claims CM seat:'Kacchi Chhori' pulled Mulayam's chair; how UP politics changed in 12 hours
summary: In politics, there are days that determine decades of the future. This story is from an era when power was based not on sharing but on bargaining. On one side, Mulayam Singh saw power as a ladder; on the other side, Kanshi Ram saw it as the key to movement. In between was Mayawati, who was first kept away, then controlled, and finally, attempts were made to eliminate her. In today's 'Political Arena', read the story of when a guest house became a battlefield and one night changed UP politics forever... October 1993, Ashoka Hotel Delhi. Room number 324, there was intense activity in the corridor outside. This room belonged to industrialist Jayant Malhotra. Two political veterans were sitting face to face in the room, Mulayam Singh Yadav and Kanshi Ram. Industrialist Sanjay Dalmia was also present. Placing a glass on the table, Dalmia said- "Mulayam ji, the enemy is big. If we fight alone, the BJP's chariot will crush everyone." Mulayam Singh looked at Kanshi Ram with his small eyes and said, "If the enemy is one, there's no harm in joining hands. But the seats...?" A mysterious smile appeared on Kanshi Ram's face. Then he said- "Mulayam ji, I'm not hungry for seats. I'm searching for that 'master key' that will unlock the fate of Dalits. You contest the election, we will support you." Malhotra smilingly interrupted- "This alliance is necessary for the country's soft landing, Kanshi Ram ji. The gap between the rich and the poor has become too wide." Samajwadi Party (SP) and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) were now in the same camp. Prime Minister Narasimha Rao had also given his blessing from behind the curtain. The strange thing was that Kanshi Ram had kept his most fierce disciple, Mayawati, away from this entire conversation. A close worker asked Kanshi Ram in a hushed voice- "Sir, didn't you call Behenji? She might feel bad." Kanshiram said in a low voice, "Mayawati has a fierce temperament. She could have broken the delicate thread of negotiation. It's better to keep her away for now." Mayawati was restricted to western UP. When the results came, there was an earthquake in the political corridors from Delhi to Lucknow. The combination of Mandal and Dalit politics had slowed down the pace of Hindutva's chariot. BJP was the largest party with 177 seats, but far from a majority. Meanwhile, SP got 109 seats, and BSP got 67 seats. This alliance was also well behind the magical number for a majority (212), but formed the government with support from Congress (28) and Janata Dal (27). Kanshiram's 10-year-old party was about to write the destiny of the country's largest state. Kanshi Ram had grabbed a part of the 'master key', but a question was still floating in the air - was this friendship out of 'compulsion' or 'necessity'...? Mulayam Singh Yadav was about to sit on the Chief Minister's chair for the first time. Out of 27 ministers, 11 were from the BSP. Kanshi Ram looked at Mayawati- "You will not join the government. You have to keep a check on the government." There was a different sparkle in Mayawati's eyes- "Don't worry, sir. The government will run on BSP's agenda. Not a single file will pass without my scrutiny." December 1993, that afternoon, Lucknow's streets were jammed. A new song was echoing in the air, which was written by a former associate of Indira Gandhi's close tantric Chandraswami, specifically at Mulayam Singh's request. Its lyrics were- "Brave Mulayam all around, Kanshi Ram's power has taken hold..." Mulayam himself had said- "The vehicle will only move forward when Kanshi Ram ji's name is in the song. It's important to keep the partner happy." This was a union of two different worlds. On one side were SP's aggressive and noisy supporters, who were dancing intoxicated with victory. On the other side were BSP people - quiet, intimidated, but with an amazing sparkle in their eyes. Even in Lucknow's harsh winter, many of them were barefoot. The foundation of this alliance rested on three different ideologies, which were merely tolerating each other. For Kanshiram, this alliance was a laboratory. He did not particularly like Mulayam's legacy. Kanshiram was confident that this UP experiment would create a stir across the country. He looked at Mayawati with a smile- "Now I will set out to tour the whole country. The command of Lucknow is in your hands. You will handle it, right...?" Mayawati assured him, saying, "Don't worry, sir. Lucknow will be in my fist." But Mulayam Singh Yadav was a seasoned player. He was called the 'wrestler' of politics. For him, this alliance was just a ladder to power. Mulayam quietly told his close associates, "Kanshiram and this girl are still raw." 'Girl' meaning Mayawati... Another move was playing out in his mind. He was confident that if not today, then tomorrow, he would break BSP's MLAs and merge them into his party and swallow Kanshi Ram's entire group. But a new echo began to be heard in the corridors of the secretariat. Mulayam Singh was certainly sitting in the Chief Minister's chair, but someone else had the real influence. Kanshi Ram had deliberately distanced himself from Uttar Pradesh affairs. He understood that his disciple was now ready to take flight. A new name emerged in newspaper headlines - "Super CM..." A journalist asked Mayawati, "Behenji, people have started calling you Super CM. Is this true?" A stern but satisfied smile appeared on Mayawati's face. She said - "The public is saying what they are seeing. BSP is the backbone of this government, and the backbone determines how the body will function." The Mandal Commission report was the adhesive between both parties. She also played the reservation card in the hilly regions of Uttarakhand. BJP and Congress leaders were left squirming - "Backward castes in the mountains are only two percent. Reservation politics there is madness." Mulayam Singh replied with his familiar smile - "We are concerned with social justice, not percentages." This alliance proved to be a lottery for Mayawati. After the defeat in 1991, Parliament seemed distant to her, but in January 1994, she was elected as a Rajya Sabha member. A supporter congratulated her, saying- "Behenji, now you will roar again in Parliament." Mayawati replied in a cold tone - "Parliament is fine, but now the real power is in Lucknow. I have to hoist BSP's flag in every district of UP." Meanwhile, the media started publishing reports that a 'cold war' had begun between Mulayam and Mayawati. Mayawati immediately took charge. In a press conference, she said- "This Manuwadi media is dancing to the BJP's tunes. There is no rift between Mulayam Singh ji. This is a conspiracy to create division." The journalist asked, "But Congress and Janata Dal are giving you unconditional support, are you calling them casteist too?" Mayawati slammed her hand on the table and said- "Supporting us is their compulsion, not a favor. Without us, they couldn't have stopped the BJP. BJP was dreaming of capturing the whole country; we have jammed the wheels of their chariot." Meanwhile, a new phrase had started circulating in the UP Secretariat - 'Behenji's order.' Mayawati liked being called the Super CM, and she proved it, too. She would often boldly say- "I don't discuss with the Chief Minister; sometimes I even give him directions." Mulayam Singh grew increasingly uneasy with Mayawati’s assertive leadership. Her demands, especially on Dalit atrocities, highlighted the coalition’s failures in social justice. Despite official mediation by PL Punia, tensions rose as backward caste violence against Dalits surged. Kanshi Ram further humiliated Mulayam Singh publicly, forcing him to wait while he appeared informally, underscoring the power struggle within the coalition. Mulayam Singh was swallowing this insult like poison. He didn't make any noise about it publicly, but internally, he started working on a dangerous plan. Mulayam Singh had realized that a direct fight would not work. He started reaching out to those old BSP veterans who were burning with jealousy over Mayawati's rising stature. The names that emerged were Dr. Masood Ahmad, Jung Bahadur Patel, and Raj Bahadur. Mulayam Singh sent his pawns - "Why are you wasting your political career behind Behenji? Come with us, you'll get both respect and power." This move of Mulayam proved successful. BSP's organization started cracking from within. MLAs were ready to defect. Kanshi Ram and Mayawati felt they were making Mulayam bend, but they didn't know that Mulayam was pulling their own ground from under their feet. The panchayat elections held in early 1995 came as a shock to Kanshi Ram and Mayawati. Mulayam Singh's SP captured 30 out of 50 districts. Congress and the BJP also grabbed some seats, but the BSP got only one district. In the intoxication of his victory, Mulayam Singh was forgetting a very big equation - the friendship between Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Kanshi Ram. When Kanshi Ram reached Parliament in 1991, Vajpayee was among the first major leaders who extended a hand of friendship. One evening, a tea session was going on at Vajpayee's bungalow. Kanshiram was sitting across. Vajpayee said with a gentle smile- "Kanshiram ji, there are no enemies in politics, only possibilities." Kanshiram replied, "Atal ji, we are in search of that master key which will unlock the fate of Dalits." Vajpayee's discerning eyes had sensed that if the BJP wanted to cross the threshold of power again in UP, Dalit support was necessary. RSS chief Rajendra Singh (Rajju Bhaiya) also endorsed this. Mulayam Singh was convinced that Hindutva and Bahujan ideology could never unite. He was confident, unaware that the death warrant of his government had already been written in Atal Bihari Vajpayee's drawing room. The summer of 1995 brought fire to Lucknow. Kanshi Ram was in a hospital bed. Old diabetes and high blood pressure had broken his body, but his mind was still working like electricity. The presence of industrialist Jayant Malhotra in that white hospital room was proof that a big game was about to unfold. Kanshi Ram played the card of his old friendship with Vajpayee. Vajpayee convinced Advani and Kalyan Singh on a plan that would pull the carpet from under Mulayam Singh's feet. Surprisingly, Mayawati had no inkling of this until the last moment. Kanshi Ram called Mayawati to the hospital. There were tears in Mayawati's eyes. Holding Kanshi Ram's hand, she said- "Sir, what will happen to us if something happens to you? Who will handle this movement?" Kanshiram signaled the nurse to go out and asked in a low voice, "Would you like to become Chief Minister?" Mayawati was stunned. She thought 'Saheb' was delirious in his illness. Kanshiram slid a bundle of files towards her and said- "Take these and go straight to the Governor. He will administer the oath to you." Afternoon of June 1, 1995 After Mayawati withdrew support and met Governor Motilal Vora, Mulayam Singh was left furious and shaken. On June 2, SP supporters stormed the State Guest House, assaulting BSP MLAs and forcing some to sign blank papers under threat. As chaos spread, several MLAs were abducted, while Mayawati and her aides barricaded themselves inside room number 1, narrowly escaping the violence. On June 2, SP supporters stormed the State Guest House, threatening Mayawati, cutting electricity and phones, and creating chaos. Brave police officers Vijay Bhushan and Subhash Singh protected her until District Magistrate Rajeev Kher arrived to disperse the crowd. The ordeal steeled Mayawati’s resolve, earning her the title “Iron Lady.” The next day, June 3, Governor Motilal Vora administered her oath as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, making her the first Dalit woman to lead the state. June 19 Assembly Speaker Dhaniram Verma declared the Governor’s removal of the Mulayam government unconstitutional and adjourned the house. SP MLAs walked out, but the remaining 275 members supported Mayawati. With Congress, BJP, Janata Dal, and rebel SP MLAs backing her, Mulayam Singh Yadav was isolated. title: UP leaders actively participate in Maharashtra civic polls:About 30 lakh UP-origin voters impact results; Samajwadi Party fields candidates in high-density migrant areas
summary: Leaders from UP made their presence felt in Maharashtra's civic elections, especially leaders from eastern UP, who campaigned extensively. The reason was that there are about 30 lakh voters from UP there. To attract these voters, many prominent leaders camped in Mumbai for several days. Voting was completed yesterday, and the results will come today. Which UP leaders reached Maharashtra? How much influence do UP people have in Maharashtra elections? Why were leaders from Azamgarh and Jaunpur so active? Read the full report... First know how important Maharashtra's local election is Jafar Azmi from Azamgarh, UP, who is active in Mumbai elections, says - There are 227 seats under BMC. Out of these, 70 seats are where people from eastern UP and Bihar live in large numbers. Samajwadi Party has fielded its candidates on all these 70 seats. Azmi says - BMC is the richest civic body. Its annual budget is 70 thousand crore rupees. In such a situation, everyone desires to become a BMC corporator (councilor). Here, generally, a candidate getting 12 to 15 thousand votes also becomes a corporator. There are several seats here where the population of people from eastern UP and Bihar is up to 30 percent. These include districts like Bhiwandi, Malat, Andheri, and Kurla. Besides, a large number of people also live in the Mumbra area of Thane. This is why UP leaders have arrived in Maharashtra in large numbers for campaigning. Tussle... There was also competition to show dominance During the Maharashtra local body elections, Purvanchal's strongman leader Dhananjay Singh was seen wearing the BJP's badge. While in UP, he raises JDU's flag. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party leader Abu Asim Azmi had called leaders from Azamgarh and surrounding districts in large numbers for party campaigning. During the campaign, there were sharp exchanges, taunts, and even instances of abuse. While addressing a meeting, Abu Asim Azmi challenged MIM leader Imtiaz Jaleel, saying 'I am from Uttar Pradesh, I will throw you down and your teeth will come out. You're going around boasting about having one MP. I have 37 MPs.' In the Maharashtra election, SP's firebrand leader and Machhlishahr MLA Ragini Sonkar, Leader of Opposition in Assembly Mata Prasad Pandey, Machhlishahr MP Priya Saroj, Kaushambi MP Pushpendra Saroj, Azamgarh MP Dharmendra Yadav, Jaunpur MP Babu Singh Kushwaha, Basti MP Ram Prasad Chaudhary, Ambedkar Nagar MLA Ram Achal Rajbhar, SP MLA Nafis Ahmad and other such leaders arrived for campaigning. Aparna Yadav also arrived for campaigning Mulayam Singh Yadav's daughter-in-law and BJP leader and Women's Commission Vice President Aparna Yadav also reached Mumbai to campaign for the BMC elections. In addition to her, BJP leaders, including Ramesh Mishra, MLA from Badlapur seat of Jaunpur district, and Ramesh Jaiswal, MLA from Mughalsarai seat of Chandauli, also reached Mumbai for campaigning. Why did Dhananjay Singh have to go to Maharashtra? Dhananjay Singh has been involved in Purvanchal politics, but this is the first time he has gone to Mumbai to campaign for the BJP and Shinde alliance leader. While Dhananjay Singh is a leader of Janata Dal United in Maharashtra, he appeared completely colored in saffron. He was also wearing a BJP band around his neck. Questions are also being raised about why Dhananjay had to enter the field despite Kripahankar Singh, one of Jaunpur's major leaders who had considerable influence in Mumbai politics. Kripahankar Singh is a senior BJP leader. He was also the BJP's candidate from Jaunpur in the last Lok Sabha elections. Dhananjay had also supported him. Why are only people from Azamgarh and Jaunpur so active? Moazzam, who has been living in Mumbai for a long time, told Dainik Bhaskar that people from two main districts of Purvanchal - Azamgarh and Jaunpur live in Mumbai in large numbers. There are many who have even built their houses and properties there. Moazzam says - Purvanchal voters have a good influence in BMC elections. They determine the win-loss on many seats. This is why big leaders from Azamgarh and Jaunpur came here to campaign in this election. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra State Chief General Secretary Meraj Siddiqui says - People from Eastern UP, or let's say North Indians, live in Mumbai in large numbers. There are many areas where it doesn't even feel like it's outside UP. According to Meraj, a large number of people from UP also contested in this election. However, when it comes to elections, we cannot ignore the conflict between the people of UP and Maharashtra. Sometimes opposition is also seen in terms of language. Maharashtra people allege that UP people are taking away their jobs. Senior journalist Anand Rai says - The opposition to North Indians in Maharashtra began during Bala Saheb Thackeray's era. However, his opposition was based on the argument that people from UP and Gujarat were taking away the rights of Maharashtra's people. His opposition continued in a very logical manner. But when Raj Thackeray's era came, he took an aggressive stance against North Indians. As a result, North Indians became organized wherever they lived across Maharashtra. A formal organization of North Indians was also formed. People from districts like Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Gorakhpur, Basti, and Gonda remained active in it. This was the reason why the influence of North Indians kept growing there. Whether it was the BMC election or the assembly election. People from here started going to create an atmosphere in favor of candidates contesting elections there.

title: Minister Mannu Kori tries to touch commissioner’s feet in Lalitpur:During overbridge inspection visit officer stops him from doing so; folds his hands, as MLA and district officials began to smile
summary: UP Minister of State Manohar Lal Panth tried to touch the feet of Jhansi Division Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey on Thursday. Seeing this, the Commissioner stopped him and folded both his hands. Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey had gone to inspect an under-construction overbridge in Lalitpur. Minister Panth arrived with a large garland to welcome Commissioner Dubey. The minister stepped forward to put on the garland, but the Commissioner put it on him instead. After this, the minister bent down to touch his feet. His hands had just reached his knees when the Commissioner stopped him and folded his hands. Seeing this unique relationship between the minister and officer, Sadar MLA Ram Ratan Kushwaha, DM Satya Prakash, and everyone present there started smiling. The minister and the commissioner were also seen smiling. Actually, on Thursday morning, Jhansi Division Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey arrived at Kelgunwa intersection on NH-44 to inspect the under-construction overbridge. Around 11:30, when the Commissioner arrived, State Minister Manohar Lal Panth and Sadar MLA Ramratan Kushwaha were also present there. The State Minister first garlanded the Sadar MLA. A little later, when the Commissioner arrived with DM Satyaprakash and SP Mohammad Mushtaq, the State Minister tried to garland him. The Commissioner took the garland and instead put it on the State Minister. After this, the State Minister attempted to touch his feet. DM said - Will soon be opened for traffic DM Satya Prakash said - The work on one lane of the bridge is almost complete. It will soon be opened for traffic. A little work is remaining, which will be completed by this evening, if not, then definitely by tomorrow. Traffic will be opened on one side of the bridge either tomorrow or day after. It will be made available to the public. Commissioner praised the State Minister and DM Commissioner Vimal Kumar Dubey said - This was one of our pending projects, which was causing a lot of inconvenience to people. The District Magistrate took cognizance of this. After that, I conducted an inspection. I congratulate the NHAI officers; they fulfilled what they had promised. Public representatives and the Minister also conducted regular visits. The DM remained continuously active. He had deployed his entire team. This is a big New Year's gift being given to the public. The bridge will be opened in a day or two.

title: Where are Shah Jahan and Mumtaz actually buried?:Real graves lie 22 feet below Taj Mahal's main dome, entry barred
summary: One of the world's most beautiful buildings, the Taj Mahal's true identity comes from its marble stones, unique inlay work with colored pearls, and beautiful architecture. Even today, these all appear to narrate the story of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz. The tombs of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz, located in the center of the main dome, are a testament to this. But do you know that these are not the real tombs of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz? Don't be surprised, the tombs that millions of tourists see every day while remembering the immortal love story are fake tombs. Actually, the real tombs are in a rectangular basement 22.2 feet deep, which is directly below the fake tombs. Dainik Bhaskar shows you through our camera the path to the real tombs and their current condition... 2 graves visible after descending 22 feet Mughal emperor Shah Jahan's 371st Urs (birthday) celebration has begun. On Thursday, ASI officials descended 22 feet into the basement at the Taj Mahal. Shah Jahan-Mumtaz's real graves were opened. After this, the Urs began with the ritual of Ghusl (applying sandalwood paste on the graves). Here lie the real graves of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz, which are in the basement below the main dome. This basement is beneath fake graves; its path also goes down through stairs in front of fake graves, which remains covered with a grating. No one can go here. During Urs, this grating was opened, and our team reached the basement after descending 21 stairs in the darkness. The real graves of Shah Jahan-Mumtaz were visible in front. Mumtaz's grave was not decorated, colored pearls were embedded on Shah Jahan's grave This basement is usually closed, but ASI employees occasionally open it for cleaning or other repair work. The basement remains closed for tourists; no one can come and go here. There is also no ventilation arrangement here, so it remains quite humid. Between the marble walls in this basement are only the real tombs of Shah Jahan-Mumtaz; nothing else is in this basement. There is no carving on its walls either. There is no decoration on Mumtaz's tomb here, whereas Shah Jahan's tomb is decorated, and it is studded with colorful pearls. Shah Jahan's tomb is 0.12 meters taller than Mumtaz's tomb. Fake decorated tombs made for tourists The height of the main dome of the Taj Mahal is 73 meters. The beautiful marble-carved tombs visible in the main hall are the fake tombs (cenotaphs) of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal. These tombs are built above the real tombs, and tourists can see them.

title: Satua Baba owns ₹50 cr ashram, luxury cars:Brother was murdered; how CM Yogi's favourite saint Santosh Tiwari turned into 'Jagadguru'
summary: Yellow attire, luxury vehicles like the Land Rover Defender and Porsche Turbo, worth crores for travelling. Branded sunglasses like Ray-Ban on the eyes. Someone who is often praised by UP CM Yogi. We are talking about Santosh Tiwari, who emerged from the small village of Masaura in Lalitpur, Bundelkhand. Santosh Tiwari is none other than Satua Baba, who has been making headlines in the Magh Mela. The elder brother who showed Satua Baba the path of spirituality 26 years ago is no longer in this world. He has been murdered. How did Santosh Tiwari reach Banaras? When did the family learn about him becoming a monk? Why did his mother insist on taking her last breath in his ashram? Read the untold stories of Satua Baba's life... Masaura village is located just 6 km away from the Lalitpur district headquarters, adjacent to National Highway-44. Santosh Tiwari alias Satua Baba is the youngest of 4 children of Shobharam Tiwari and his wife Raja Beti Tiwari, who live here. The eldest is Mahesh Tiwari, followed by Neeraj and Umesh Tiwari. Mahesh Tiwari is no longer in this world. He was murdered in 2007. Mahesh was the person who took Santosh Tiwari from Lalitpur to the Banaras ashram. Went to study in Banaras at age 13 Santosh Tiwari, alias Satua Baba's elder brother, Umesh Tiwari told Dainik Bhaskar that this was in the year 2000. He had passed 9th grade. At that time, he was barely 13 years old. Instead of regular studies, Santosh wanted to pursue spiritual education. So our elder brother, Mahesh Tiwari, took him to Manikarnika Ghat in Banaras. Bathed in the Ganges there. Nearby was the Satua Ashram. Here, too, there was a facility for Vedic Gurukul education. Santosh told his elder brother to get him admitted to this ashram. After this, they took Santosh to Satua Ashram. There, they met the head priest, Yamunacharya Maharaj of the ashram. He handed over his younger brother to him and said that from today, he is under your protection. Other children like him were also staying in the ashram to study. Santosh became one of the favorite disciples of the Mahant Umesh Tiwari recalls that Santosh Tiwari joined an ashram for studies and often came home during holidays. He quickly learned religious texts and became a favourite disciple of the Mahant. Around 2005, Santosh casually informed the family that he was taking sannyasa, which they initially dismissed as a joke. Days later, priests from Varanasi confirmed that he had renounced worldly life. The news deeply shocked the family, especially his mother, who questioned the Mahant. Though the Mahant tried to explain, the decision left Santosh’s parents grieving and worried about his future for the rest of their lives. Satua Baba's father, mother, and sister-in-law have also passed away Santosh Tiwari, alias Satua Baba's father, Shobharam Tiwari, passed away in 2019, and his elder brother Mahesh Tiwari's wife, Manisha Tiwari, died in 2023. Manisha Tiwari had served as the village head until 2021. In 2023, Santosh Tiwari's mother, Raja Beti Tiwari, also passed away. She took her last breath in Satua Baba's ashram. In her final moments, her great desire was to spend some time with her younger son, Santosh Tiwari. By then, Santosh Tiwari had become the head priest of this monastery. Currently, the families of all three elder brothers of Satua Baba are living separately in the village. All have built luxurious houses. The younger son of the eldest brother works as an accountant at Baba Ramdev's ashram in Haridwar. While the elder son is an outsourced worker at the block. Umesh Tiwari said that Santosh Tiwari got the village temple renovated by speaking with the tourism department. The last time they came to the village was in 2023 to attend their mother's thirteenth-day ritual. Became Mahamandaleshwar while Guru was still alive Yamunacharya Ji Maharaj declared Santosh Tiwari his successor and Mahamandaleshwar before his death in 2011. Since then, Santosh Tiwari has been managing the monastery and is known as Satua Baba. The Satua Peeth owns properties in several states, including Gujarat, and Satua Baba’s influence has steadily grown. In Mahakumbh-2025, he was anointed Jagadguru by Jagadguru Rambhadracharya in the presence of CM Yogi and senior saints. Satua Baba is the 57th Acharya of the Vishnu Swami Sampradaya, a lineage that began over 2,600 years ago and has continued through successive Mahants at the Satua Baba Ashram. Once ascetics in ashram used to drink sattu, today they have luxury cars worth crores There's also a story behind the name 'Satua Baba'. In 1998, the financial condition of Vishnu Peeth was quite miserable. At that time, there wasn't even a proper arrangement for food in the monastery. The ascetics survived only by drinking sattu. This is how this name came into circulation. Santosh Das, alias Satua Baba himself, says that 'Satua Baba' is not a personal name, but rather a prestigious position of the head priest in Vishnu Peeth. The ashram where ascetics once survived on sattu, today, the luxury life of its head priest is making headlines. In Banaras, this ashram has now spread over a large area. Its current value is said to be 50 crores. This monastery also has several properties in Gujarat. Those are also said to be worth crores. A luxury car worth 3 crores is parked outside Satua Baba's camp at the Magh Mela. The number UK 08 BG 8009 is from Uttarakhand, but it has Vishnu Swami Jagadguru Satua Baba Kashi written on it. Its on-road price is said to be more than 3 crores. Similarly, there is a luxury car like Porsche, which is said to be priced at 4.40 crores. Rule to report donations or property received This ashram is primarily an ancient religious seat of the Vishnu Swami sect, which operates through the guru-disciple tradition. According to the ashram's website, shrisatuababa.com, no trust deed, society number, 80G/12A certificate, or government registration details are publicly available. Property and operations run on donations from devotees. Senior High Court lawyer Jayendra Singh says that when it comes to rules, religious monasteries' property is monitored by the state government or the endowment board. When receiving large properties, it is often necessary to give notice or obtain permission.
